set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Five identical spheres are placed between two blocks in order to measure their diameter.
  What is the diameter of a single sphere?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The spheres start at the 5 cm mark and finish at the 16 cm mark. Therefore, 5 spheres are 16 - 5 = 11 cm long.
 • A single sphere is, therefore,   cm  = 2.2 cm in diameter.
 B ,  C   and D are incorrect as  the ruler has been misread, or the diameter has been wrongly calculated.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which distance-time graph shows an object moving with constant speed?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
Answer  B  is correct because:
  • On a distance-time graph, constant speed is shown by a non-horizontal straight line
 • This shows that the distance travelled per unit time is increasing at a steady rate
 • Therefore, the only correct graph is graph  B
 | A  is incorrect as
 |  A horizontal line shows that distance is not changing over time, therefore the object is  stationary
 |
 | C  is incorrect as
 |  
 An upward curved line shows that the distance travelled over time is increasing. The object is speeding up or  accelerating
 |
 | D  is incorrect as
 |  A curve like this shows that the distance travelled over time is decreasing. The object is slowing down or  decelerating
 |

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row in the table gives the correct units for mass and for weight?
 |  
 | Mass
 | Weight
 |
 | A
 | kg
 | kg
 |
 | B
 | N
 | kg
 |
 | C
 | N
 | N
 |
 | D
 | kg
 | N
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The unit of weight (a force) is the Newton, N.
 • The unit of mass is the kilogram, kg.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Four speed-time graphs have axes with the same scales. Each large square has a height of 1 m/s and width of 1 s.
  Which graph shows the greatest distance covered?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The area under a speed-time graph represents distance
 • Consider graph  A :
 • Split the area into a triangle and a rectangle 
 • Area = (½ × 5 × 5) + (3 × 5) = 27.5 
 • Consider graph  B :
 • Split the area into a rectangle and triangle
 • Area = (8 × 1) + (½ × 5 × 5) = 20.5 
 • Consider graph  C :
 • Split the area into approximately one quarter of a circle and a rectangle
 • Area ≈ (¼ × π × 5 2 ) + (3 × 5) = 34.6
 • Consider graph  D :
 • Area = (8 × 4) = 32
 • The largest area is under graph  C
 • With more complicated graph shapes, a good tactic is to  split  the area under a curve into recognisable shapes -  triangles ,  rectangles  and even sections of  circles

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Some unknown liquid in a beaker has a mass of 200 g and a volume of 230 cm 3 .
 The density of water is 1.0 g/cm 3
 How does the density of the unknown liquid compare with the density of water?
options: A. Its density is greater than the density of water
B. Its density is less than the density of water
C. Its density is the same as the density of water
D. With the information given, it is impossible to tell.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • 
 • Density = 200 / 230 = 0.87 g/cm 3
 • This is less than 1.0 g/cm 3
 A  is incorrect as the density is less than the density of water.
 C  is incorrect as the density is less than the density of water.
 D  is incorrect as it is possible to tell what the density is.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A motorbike travels at a constant speed along a flat road. Three horizontal forces act on the motorbike. Two of them are shown in the diagram below.
  What is the size and direction of the third force?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • The motorbike is travelling at a constant speed 
 • This means that the resultant force on it must be 0 N
 • The resultant force on the motorbike (before the third unknown force is added) is 
 • 2000 - 800 = 1200 N forwards
 • Therefore, a force of  1200 N backwards  is required to give a resultant force of 0 N
 A  is incorrect as this would give a resultant force of 4000 N forwards.
 C  is incorrect as this would give a resultant force of 2400 N forwards.
 D  is incorrect as this would give a resultant force of 1600 N backwards.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagrams below show three beams, each is pivoted at the centre. Each beam also has two forces acting on it, as shown.
  Which of the beams will rotate clockwise?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • If the beam is to rotate clockwise, the  clockwise moment must be greater than the anticlockwise moment.
 • Moment = force x distance from pivot
 • The forces on the right of the beams turn them clockwise, while those on the left turn them anticlockwise.
 • In no case is force x distance on the right greater than force x distance on the left.
 For X:
 • anticlockwise force = 3.0 m x 4.0 N = 12 N/m
 • clockwise force = 2.0 m x 4.0 N = 8 N/m
 • = turns anticlockwise (left)
 For Y:
 • anticlockwise force = 6.0 m x 4.0 N = 24 N/m
 • clockwise force = 2.0 m x 8.0 N = 16 N/m
 • = turns anticlockwise (left)
 For Z:
 • anticlockwise force = 3.0 m x 5.0 N = 15 N/m
 • clockwise force = 6.0 m x 2.0 N = 12 N/m
 • = turns anticlockwise (left)
  
 • None of the beams rotate clockwise.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A wardrobe is shown tilted at a variety of angles.
  In which position is the wardrobe in equilibrium?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • For equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero, and the resultant moment must be zero.
 • In this question, we need only deal with the resultant moment.
 • The centre of mass is directly over the pivot point, so the distance of the weight from the pivot is zero, this means the moment is zero.
 • Therefore, the wardrobe is in equilibrium (though a tiny force would tip it away from equilibrium)
 A  is incorrect as the weight makes an anticlockwise moment. The wardrobe would tip anticlockwise
 B  is incorrect as the weight makes a clockwise moment about the pivot. The wardrobe would tip clockwise.
 D  is incorrect as the weight makes a clockwise moment about the pivot. The wardrobe would tip clockwise.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which energy source relies on radiation from the Sun?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Plants form the basis for fossil fuels
 • Plants grow using  radiation  from the  Sun
 Geothermal energy relies on the  heat  produced in the Earth's core and radioactive elements in the crust.
 Nuclear power relies on the energy released by  radioactive   materials
 Tidal power comes (mostly) from the gravitational attraction to the Moon. Some of this is influenced by the Sun, but  not  by its  radiation .

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following energy transfers is most efficient?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The most efficient energy transfer is the one that produces the greatest percentage of  useful energy output , which is the same as saying the  lowest percentage of wasted energy  output
 • Answer  D  has a wasted energy output of  25%
 • Therefore, it has a useful energy output of  75%
 • Answer  D  has the greatest percentage of useful energy output
 • Therefore, it is the most efficient energy transfer

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A briefcase, with flat, rectangular sides rests on the floor as shown in the diagram.
  The briefcase is now turned so that it rests with its large, flat side on the floor.
  How has the change affected the force on the floor, and the pressure exerted by the briefcase on the floor?
 |  
 | Force
 | Pressure
 |
 | A
 | unchanged
 | decreased
 |
 | B
 | unchanged
 | unchanged
 |
 | C
 | decreased
 | decreased
 |
 | D
 | decreased
 | unchanged
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The  force  on the floor is caused by the  weight  of the briefcase, weight is the force, due to gravity, that pulls the briefcase downward. The briefcase’s weight does not change, so the force is  unchanged .
 • Pressure = Force / Area, the  area  of the briefcase in contact with the floor has  increased . This means that the pressure has decreased.
 B  is incorrect as the pressure is not unchanged, it has decreased.
 C  and  D  are incorrect as the force remains the same.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A small metal block is suspended under the surface of a beaker of water by a string. 
 The metal block experiences a pressure exerted by the liquid.
   What would increase the pressure exerted on the metal block?
options: A. increasing the surface area of the stone
B. using a liquid with a lower density
C. increasing the mass of the metal block
D. lowering the metal block deeper into the liquid
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Lowering the block deeper into the liquid would  increase  the pressure
 A  is incorrect as surface area has no effect on pressure in a fluid.
 B  is incorrect as lowering the density would  reduce  the pressure.
 C  is incorrect as mass of the block has no effect on the pressure in a fluid.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A popular demonstration of kinetic theory is to view smoke particles through a microscope, while illuminating them with a bright light.
 The diagram shows the view of the smoke particles through a microscope. They are moving about randomly.
  What causes the motion of the smoke particles?
options: A. The smoke particles are attracted to each other.
B. The smoke particles vibrate because they are warm.
C. Smaller air particles are colliding with the smoke particles.
D. The microscope is vibrating slightly, making the smoke particles  appear  to move.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • This random motion of smoke particles is called  Brownian motion .
 • Smoke particles are constantly being buffeted around by tiny air particles, which are too small to see with a microscope.
 • This is what causes their  random  motion.
 A  is incorrect as the smoke particles are not attracted to each other. If they had an electric charge, it is likely they would all have the same charge, and would repel anyway. This is not happening.
 B  is incorrect as the random vibration due to thermal energy is taking place in the atoms which make up the smoke particles, this would not be visible under a microscope.
 D  is incorrect as if the microscope were vibrating like this,  all  the smoke particles would appear to move in the same direction at the same time. They do not do this.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram represents particles of a gas inside a closed container of constant volume. 
  The gas is heated. 
 What happens to the particles of the gas?
options: C. They hit the container walls with less force.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D because:
 • Heating a gas increases the kinetic energy of its particles
 • A greater kinetic energy corresponds to an increase in speed
 • Therefore, the particles of the gas move faster
 A  is incorrect as the particles themselves do not change shape
 B  is incorrect as the volume of the gas is unchanged so the average separation of particles is unaffected
 C  is incorrect as the particles hit the walls with more force, as they collide with a greater speed

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The water in outdoor swimming pools gradually evaporates.
 How does the process of evaporation affect the temperature of the water in the swimming pool and what is the effect on the average kinetic energy of the water molecules?
 |  
 | Temperature
 | Average kinetic energy per molecule
 |
 | A
 | reduces
 | reduces
 |
 | B
 | stays the same
 | stays the same
 |
 | C
 | increases
 | increases
 |
 | D
 | reduces
 | stays the same
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Evaporation happens when the most energetic particles leave the surface of the swimming pool.
 • As these particles leave, they take their energy with them.
 Since temperature is the average kinetic energy per molecule in a substance, the removal of this energy causes the  average kinetic energy to fall , thus  reducing the temperature
 B  is incorrect as temperature does not stay the same when evaporation takes place.
 C  is incorrect as temperature does not increase when evaporation takes place.
 D  is incorrect as if temperature falls, the average kinetic energy per molecule must also fall, it cannot stay the same.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A car tyre is inflated with air.
 As the car drives, the temperature of the tyre increases, which also causes the temperature of the air inside the tyre to increase. This increases the pressure of the air inside the tyre.
 Which of the following is a correct explanation as to why?
options: A. The mass of air inside the tyre has increased.
B. The area of the tyre has decreased, thus increasing the pressure.
C. The air molecules collide with each other less frequently.
D. The average kinetic energy of the air molecules has increased.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy (KE) per molecule. If the  temperature increases , then so does the average KE per molecule.
 • If the particles have  more KE , they move with a  greater velocity . This causes them to hit the walls of the tyre at a greater speed, and to  exert  more  force  when they bounce off.
 • This increased force  increases  the  pressure  in the tyre.
 A  is incorrect as the tyre has not been pumped up, so no more air has been added. Therefore the mass cannot have increased.
 B  is incorrect as the tyre has a (very nearly) fixed volume therefore the area with which air molecules can collide could not have changed.
 C  is incorrect as if anything, the molecules will collide with each other  more  frequently, but it is collisions with the wall of the  tyre  that increase the pressure.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
In a very common classroom Physics demonstration, a teacher sets up a rod, as shown in the diagram. Half of the rod is copper, the other half is wood.
 She sticks four lead balls to the rod using wax. The wax melts when its temperature rises a small amount, causing the ball to fall off.
  The teacher heats the rod in the centre, with something more gentle than a Bunsen burner, that will not burn the wood.
 Which ball falls off first?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Copper is a significantly better  conductor  of heat than wood.
 • This means that the heat will be conducted towards balls B and A more quickly than it will towards C and D.
 • Since ball B is closest to the heat source, its wax will melt first, and it will be the first to fall
 A  is incorrect as  A  is further from the heat source than  B
 C  is incorrect as wood is a worse conductor of heat than copper
 D  is incorrect as wood is a worse conductor of heat than copper and the ball is further from the heat source.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A lit match is placed above a thermometer.
  Which row in the table shows how the thermal energy from the lit match reaches the thermometer?
 |  
 | Convection
 | Conduction
 | Radiation
 |
 | A
 | yes
 | yes
 | yes
 |
 | B
 | yes
 | yes
 | no
 |
 | C
 | no
 | yes
 | yes
 |
 | D
 | no
 | no
 | yes
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Air is a terrible thermal conductor.
 • Convection only transfers heat in an upwards direction, and the thermometer is being held  beneath  the match.
 • Infrared radiation is emitted equally in all directions, so this is the only one that can reach the match.
 Always look for a  direction  when dealing with convection questions.  Convection  always transfers heat  upwards .

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the definition of the word  amplitude ?
options: A. The number of complete waves that pass a point per second.
B. The distance from the peak of one wave to the peak of an adjacent wave.
C. The distance from the equilibrium position of a peak plus the same distance from a trough.
D. The maximum distance from the equilibrium position of any point on a wave.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Amplitude is shown on the diagram, as is wavelength.
 • Amplitude is the maximum distance from the equilibrium position of any point on a wave.
  A  is incorrect as this is the definition of frequency.
 B  is incorrect as this is the definition of wavelength.
 C  is incorrect as this is the standard error made by students when defining amplitude.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the name given to the effect that allows the wavefronts to reach point X, shown on the diagram?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C   because   diffraction is the name given to the spreading out of waves as they pass through a gap, as shown in the diagram below.
  A  is incorrect as reflection is what happens when waves bounce off a boundary.
 B  is incorrect as refraction is what happens when waves change speed and (usually) direction when they cross a boundary.
 D  is incorrect as dispersion is the spreading out of the different colours of (usually) light when they are passed through a prism.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A teacher has a clock mounted in such a way that students can only see its reflection in a plane mirror.
 The diagram shows the reflection of the clock.
  What time is shown on the clock?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D   because images in a plane mirror are always reflected left to right but not top to bottom.
 This diagram shows the actual clock:

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A physics teacher demonstrates dispersion for her class. She asks the students to draw a diagram of the dispersion.
 The diagrams show four examples of what different students drew. One of them is correct. Which one?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Light has to disperse a little as it passes through the prism.
 • Light has to refract in the correct direction: towards the normal on the way in and away from the normal on the way out.
 A  is incorrect as light refracts in the wrong direction, and it does not disperse at all inside the prism.
 C  is incorrect as the light does not disperse in the prism, though it does refract in the right direction.
 D  is incorrect as light does disperse in the prism, but refracts in the wrong direction.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the images correctly shows the focal length of the thin converging lens?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because the focal length is the distance from the lens at which parallel light rays would converge. This is shown in diagram B.
 The other answers do not label the focal length correctly.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following types of electromagnetic radiation has the highest speed in a vacuum?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because: 
 all  types of electromagnetic radiation travel at  the same  speed in a vacuum.
 That speed is the speed of light: 3 x 10 8  m/s.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The speed of a wave is doubled. The frequency remains the same.
 What happens to the wavelength of the wave?
options: D. It becomes four times as large
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The wave equation    applies here.
 • Rearrange   : 
 • If  v  doubles, and  f  stays the same:    
 •   is twice as big as   , the original wavelength.
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not get the algebra correct.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the lists of metals below contains only metals which are non-ferrous?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • A ferrous metal contains  iron , a non-ferrous metal does not.
 • Aluminium and copper are elements, so they cannot contain iron.
 • Brass is an alloy of copper and tin, which does not contain iron.
 A  is incorrect as iron is ferrous, and steel is an alloy of iron.
 B  is incorrect as steel is an alloy of iron, which is ferrous.
 D  is incorrect as iron is ferrous.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about a permanent bar magnet is  incorrect ?
options: A. The S-pole attracts the N-pole of another magnet
B. The S-pole repels the S-pole of another magnet
C. It cannot repel a non-magnetic material
D. It is made from a soft magnetic material (such as soft iron)
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The incorrect statement is  D  because:
 • A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field
 • This means it never loses its magnetism
 • Most permanent magnets are made from 'hard' iron, nickel, or cobalt
 • A soft magnetic material, such as soft iron, will only be magnetic whilst there is a current around it (such as in an electromagnet)
 • Once the current is switched off, it is demagnetised (loses its magnetism)
 • This means it wouldn't work as a permanent magnet
 A  is correct as opposite poles attract, so an S-pole will attract the N-pole of another magnet
 B  is correct as like poles repel, so an S-pole will repel the S-pole of another magnet
 C  is correct as permanent magnets can only attract or repel other magnetic materials, so it is true that they cannot repel non-magnetic materials

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A PVC (plastic) rod is rubbed with a nylon cloth. This process causes electrons to be transferred between the rod and the cloth, causing both objects to become charged.
 Which row gives the correct nature of the charges on both the cloth and the rod, and the effect the objects have on each other after becoming charged?
 |  
 | Charges on rod and cloth
 | Effect
 |
 | A
 | the same
 | repel
 |
 | B
 | the same
 | attract
 |
 | C
 | opposite
 | repel
 |
 | D
 | opposite
 | attract
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • When the rod is rubbed with the cloth, electrons are transferred between them
 • If electrons move from the cloth, the cloth becomes positive
 • If electrons move to the rod, the rod becomes negative
 • This means the two objects have  opposite  charges
 • Opposite charges  attract
 A  and  B  are incorrect as the charges will be opposite.
 C  is incorrect as opposite charges will attract, not repel.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A 2.0 Ω resistor is connected to meter X and meter Y as shown in the diagram.
  Which row in the table shows possible values for the two meters?
 |  
 | X
 | Y
 |
 | A
 | 4.0
 | 8.0
 |
 | B
 | 2.0
 | 2.0
 |
 | C
 | 4.0
 | 2.0
 |
 | D
 | 1.0
 | 1.0
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • This one is tricky, because you are not given very much information; you have to work out a lot.
 • Meter  X is connected in series with the resistor , this means it has to be an ammeter, and is measuring current.
 • Meter  Y is connected in parallel with the resistor , this means it has to be a voltmeter and is measuring voltage.
 • We know that    and the only combination of  V  and  I  that gives us a resistance of 2.0 ᘯ is 8.0 V and 4.0 A.
 The tricksy answer is  C , because the values would give the correct answer  if  they were reversed.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows a toaster that has been wired up.
 Three fuses have been connected to the toaster, but only one or two have been connected correctly.
  Which of the fuses has been positioned correctly?
options: A. Fuse X and fuse Y
D. Fuse X and fuse Z
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because: 
 • A fuse must be connected in series with the live wire. Only fuse  X  is in the correct position.
 A  is incorrect as fuse  Y  is in series with the  neutral  wire. It is in the wrong position.
 C  is incorrect as fuse  Z  is connected in parallel with the heating element. This is really badly in the wrong position, would cause a short circuit, and would blow fuse  Z  as soon as the circuit was switched on.
 D  is incorrect as  X  is in the correct position but  Z  is badly positioned, in parallel with the heating element. It would cause a short circuit, and would blow fuse  Z  as soon as the circuit was switched on

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: This is the circuit symbol for which component?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D because:
 • This is the circuit symbol for a relay.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An oven is wired into somebody’s kitchen. The oven is protected by a fuse, and functions normally, but the owner notices that the wires that connect the oven to the mains electricity supply get quite hot.
 What could be done to reduce the temperature of the wires?
options: Add a circuit breaker to the circuit.
B. Put thicker insulation on the wires.
C. Replace the wires with thicker diameter wires.
D. Replace the wires with thinner diameter wires.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The problem here is that the wires used to connect the oven are not rated for the amount of current the oven uses. This is an easy mistake to make, as ovens use more current than normal electrical devices.
 • Thicker diameter wires are required, since thicker wires have a smaller resistance, and therefore dissipate less heat when current flows through them. Remember:    gives the power dissipated by a component which has resistance.
 A  is incorrect as this would have no effect, as the oven is operating properly.
 B  is incorrect as thicker insulation might cause the wires to  feel  cooler, but they would still be just as hot. They would actually be less able to dissipate the heat they are generating, and are in greater danger of causing a fire.
 D  is incorrect as thinner wires would exacerbate the problem. They have a higher resistance, and would dissipate more heat, becoming even hotter.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, an e.m.f. is induced in the wire.
 Which of the following devices uses this effect?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, the induced e.m.f. can be used to drive a current
 • The combination of current and voltage can deliver electrical power to devices ( P  =  IV ), which causes them to work
 • This is the process used by a generator to produce electricity
 A  is incorrect as an electric motor works using the reverse effect: when a current is passed through a wire in a magnetic field, it experiences a force.
 C  is incorrect as a photon accelerator is a fictitious device, popularised on a children’s TV show in the early 90s called “Bucky O’Hare”. One might argue that a light bulb accelerates photons.
 D  is incorrect as a transformer uses the induction effect, but does not use a moving wire, it uses an alternating magnetic field to create the same effect.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
After electricity is generated at a power station, the voltage is increased significantly for transmission across the country via the national grid.
 What is the advantage of transmitting electricity at very high voltages?
options: A. It makes the electricity flow more quickly.
B. It increases the efficiency of the electricity transfer.
D. It is safer to transmit electricity at high voltage.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Since  P  =  IV , when the voltage increases, the current decreases
 • This is because the electrical power must be the same before and after transforming, otherwise, you create or destroy energy, which is not possible
 • The lower the current, the less power is dissipated as heat in the power lines
 • If less power is wasted, the transmission is more efficient
 A  is incorrect as electricity does not flow more or less quickly due to the voltage.
 C  is incorrect as power cannot be created or destroyed due to the conservation of energy. If the voltage goes up, the current comes down to compensate, since  P  =  IV.
 D  is incorrect as high voltage transmission is much  less  safe than low voltage transmission, but the rewards are worth the risk.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A transformer has 1200 turns on its secondary coil and has an output voltage of 240 V.
  If the input voltage is 12 V, how many turns are there on the primary coil?

The correct answer is  B  because:

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows two bar magnets, stored with metal keepers across the ends. The keepers help to keep the magnets magnetised.
  The material used for the keepers becomes strongly magnetised when placed in contact with the magnets, but does not remain magnetised when taken away from the magnets.
 What is a suitable metal to use for the magnets and what is a suitable metal to use for the keepers?
  
 |  
 | Metal for keeper
 | Metal for magnet
 |
 | A
 | steel
 | steel
 |
 | B
 | iron
 | steel
 |
 | C
 | steel
 | iron
 |
 | D
 | iron
 | iron
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Steel is slow to be magnetised (as it is an alloy of iron), and can retain its magnetism for a while
 • This makes it a good material for a magnet
 • Iron can be magnetised and demagnetised very quickly
 • This means it becomes strongly magnetised when placed in contact with the magnets, but does not remain magnetised when taken away from the magnets
 • This makes it a good material for the keeper
 Steel is often known as a 'hard' magnetic material and iron as a 'soft' magnetic material due to the relative amount of time they remain magnetised.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An atom consists of electrons orbiting a nucleus. The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.
 For the atom to be neutral, which statement about the atom  must  be correct?
options: A. The number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
B. The number of protons is equal to the number of neutrons.
C. The number of electrons, protons and neutrons are all different.
D. The number of electrons is equal to the number of neutrons.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Protons have a charge of +1. Electrons have a charge of -1.
 • For an atom to be  neutral , the  positive  charges and  negative  charges must be  equal . Therefore the number of protons must be the same as the number of electrons.
 B  and  D  are incorrect as neutrons have no charge so do not affect the overall charge of the atom.
 C  is incorrect as atoms can have different numbers of neutrons and still be neutral.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What creates the periodic nature of the seasons?
options: A. The tilting of the Earth's axis
B. The orbiting of the Earth around the Sun
C. The combination of the orbiting of the Earth around the Sun and the Earth's tilting axis
D. The change in temperature of the Sun
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The tilting of the Earth's axis means that certain hemispheres (halves) of the Earth tilt towards the Sun for one half of the year, and away from the Sun from the other half
 • When the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, this is spring and summer
 • When it is tilted away from the Sun, this is autumn and winter
 • The orbiting of the Earth around the Sun means that different sides of the Earth face the Sun at different parts of the year, every 365 days
 • Therefore, the combination of both creates the seasons
 The tilting of the Earth's axis and its orbit around the Sun is why when it is winter in Europe (in the northern hemisphere), it is summer in Australia (in the southern hemisphere). Whilst Europe is facing away from the Sun during that time, this means Australia is facing towards the Sun, because of the tilt.

 A  is incorrect as the Universe is a collection of galaxies.
 B  is incorrect as stars make up galaxies.
 D  is incorrect as a nebula is a cloud of dust and gas.

 • Place the metal in water (in the cylinder and completely submerge);  [1 mark]

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A cannonball is dropped from a three story building. 
 Which row of the table correctly describes both the speed and the acceleration of the cannonball as it falls?
 You can ignore air resistance for this question.
 |  
 | Speed
 | Acceleration
 |
 | A
 | constant
 | constant
 |
 | B
 | increasing
 | constant
 |
 | C
 | increasing
 | increasing
 |
 | D
 | constant
 | increasing
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is B because:
 • All objects in a gravitational field accelerate at the same rate
 • This rate is 9.8 m/s2 on Earth, but it is different on different planets
 • Since the cannon ball accelerates at a constant rate, its speed must be increasing because acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time
 A  is incorrect as if the speed were constant the cannon ball would not speed up as it falls
 C  is incorrect as the acceleration of falling objects does not increase, it is constant
 D  is incorrect as if the speed remained constant, then no acceleration would be taking place

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A car is driving around a circular track at a constant speed.
 Which statement describes the motion of the car?
options: A. The car is accelerating because its speed is changing
B. The car is not accelerating as it is moving at a constant speed
C. The car is accelerating because its velocity is changing
D. The car is not accelerating, but its velocity is changing.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because
 • This is a  circular motion question .
 • Velocity is defined as the speed in a given direction, if either the speed or the direction change, then the velocity changes.
 • Acceleration  is defined as the  rate of change of velocity . If the velocity changes then there must be an acceleration.
 • Since the direction changes, the velocity changes and the car is accelerating.
 A  is incorrect as the car  is  accelerating, but speed is just the size of the velocity, this is remaining constant. The  direction  is changing.
 B  is incorrect as the car  is  accelerating, as discussed above.
 D  is incorrect as by definition, if the velocity changes, the car accelerates.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

options: A. Its density is greater than the density of water
B. Its density is less than the density of water
C. Its density is the same as the density of water
D. With the information given, it is impossible to tell.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • 
 • Density = 200 / 230 = 0.87 g/cm 3
 • This is less than 1.0 g/cm 3
 A  is incorrect as the density is less than the density of water.
 C  is incorrect as the density is less than the density of water.
 D  is incorrect as it is possible to tell what the density is.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
After a car crash the car driver's airbag inflates. The airbag then deflates when it is hit by the driver’s head. 
 How does an airbag reduce the risk of injury?
options: A. Collision time increases, which increases the rate of change of momentum.
B. Collision time increases, which reduces the rate of change of momentum.
Collision time decreases, which increases the rate of change of momentum.
D. Collision time decreases, which reduces the rate of change of momentum .
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because: 
 Airbags are designed to increase the time taken for the momentum of the head to reduce to zero which subsequently reduces the force exerted on the head.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows a door handle with three forces acting on it.
  How will the door handle move?
options: C. It will move to the left.
D. It will not move at all.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 • Moment = force x distance from pivot.
 • The moment turning the handle clockwise is the largest, as the force is acting at the greatest distance from the pivot.
 B  is incorrect as the force turning the handle anticlockwise is closer to the pivot, therefore its moment will be smaller.
 C  is incorrect as the force pushing the handle to the left would be balanced by a force pushing back from the pivot, which is fixed in position.
 D  is incorrect as the handle will move as the clockwise moment is greater than the anticlockwise moment.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A wardrobe is shown tilted at a variety of angles.
  In which position is the wardrobe in equilibrium?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • For equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero, and the resultant moment must be zero.
 • In this question, we need only deal with the resultant moment.
 • The centre of mass is directly over the pivot point, so the distance of the weight from the pivot is zero, this means the moment is zero.
 • Therefore, the wardrobe is in equilibrium (though a tiny force would tip it away from equilibrium)
 A  is incorrect as the weight makes an anticlockwise moment. The wardrobe would tip anticlockwise
 B  is incorrect as the weight makes a clockwise moment about the pivot. The wardrobe would tip clockwise.
 D  is incorrect as the weight makes a clockwise moment about the pivot. The wardrobe would tip clockwise.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A rollercoaster moving along a track has a large momentum. 
 A second rollercoaster has half the mass of the first rollercoaster and travels at four times the speed.
 What is the momentum of the second rollercoaster compared to the first?
options: A. The second rollercoaster has a momentum of zero
B. The second rollercoaster's momentum is half that of the first rollercoaster's momentum
C. The second rollercoaster's momentum is twice that of the first rollercoaster's momentum
D. The second rollercoaster's momentum is four times that of the first rollercoaster's momentum
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Compare the mass and velocity of each rollercoaster:
 • The first rollercoaster has mass  m  and velocity  v
 • The second rollercoaster has mass ½ m  and velocity 4 v
 • Momentum = mass x velocity, or p =  m  x  v
 • The momentum of the first rollercoaster is  p  =  m  x  v  =  mv
 • The momentum of the second rollercoaster is  p  = (½ m ) x (4 v ) = 2 mv
 • Therefore, the momentum of the second rollercoaster will be  twice  that of the first rollercoaster's momentum

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The particles in a liquid are in contact with each other, while those in a gas are considerably further apart.
 • The average kinetic energy of each molecule is related to the temperature of the substance. This means that, if a substance has a higher temperature, its molecules will, on average, have a higher kinetic energy.
 • As Kinetic energy =   , the speed of the molecules will also be greater.
 • Since both the liquid water and the gaseous water are  both  at a temperature of 100  o C, their molecules both have  the same  kinetic energy, and are travelling at  the same  speed.
 Each of the other answers has made at least one error. Liquid particles are  always  closer together than gas particles.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A car tyre is inflated with air.
 As the car drives, the temperature of the tyre increases, which also causes the temperature of the air inside the tyre to increase. This increases the pressure of the air inside the tyre.
 Which of the following is a correct explanation as to why?
options: A. The mass of air inside the tyre has increased.
B. The area of the tyre has decreased, thus increasing the pressure.
C. The air molecules collide with each other less frequently.
D. The average kinetic energy of the air molecules has increased.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy (KE) per molecule. If the  temperature increases , then so does the average KE per molecule.
 • If the particles have  more KE , they move with a  greater velocity . This causes them to hit the walls of the tyre at a greater speed, and to  exert  more  force  when they bounce off.
 • This increased force  increases  the  pressure  in the tyre.
 A  is incorrect as the tyre has not been pumped up, so no more air has been added. Therefore the mass cannot have increased.
 B  is incorrect as the tyre has a (very nearly) fixed volume therefore the area with which air molecules can collide could not have changed.
 C  is incorrect as if anything, the molecules will collide with each other  more  frequently, but it is collisions with the wall of the  tyre  that increase the pressure.

 • Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 ℃.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 Which ball falls off first?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Copper is a significantly better  conductor  of heat than wood.
 • This means that the heat will be conducted towards balls B and A more quickly than it will towards C and D.
 • Since ball B is closest to the heat source, its wax will melt first, and it will be the first to fall
 A  is incorrect as  A  is further from the heat source than  B
 C  is incorrect as wood is a worse conductor of heat than copper
 D  is incorrect as wood is a worse conductor of heat than copper and the ball is further from the heat source.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 B  is incorrect as a still day will not increase the rate of evaporation, although the high temperature will.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following statements about energy transfer is correct?
options: A. Metals conduct thermal energy well because their electrons are not free to move.
B. Infrared radiation cannot travel through a vacuum.
C. Warm fluids rise because their particles move further apart.
D. Convection only occurs in gases.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C because:

 • Higher temperature particles are further apart, on average, and this reduces the density of the fluid, causing it to rise.
 A  is incorrect as some electrons in metals  are  free to move, which makes them good conductors.
 B  is incorrect as infrared radiation is the only means of transferring thermal energy through a vacuum.
 D  is incorrect as convection can happen in liquids or gases.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 • Medical scanning of organs and soft tissues
 • Radar systems to find distance and velocity
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:

 • Ultrasound is used to find breaks in materials such as the steel of railway lines, where an echo will reflect off a broken surface, indicating the distance to the damaged part
 • Option  1  is correct
 • In situations where x-rays would be too damaging, such as scans of the fetus or soft tissues, ultrasound is extensively used
 • Option  2  is correct
 • Radar  stands for  radio detection and ranging  and uses radio waves, not sound waves, to detect distances and velocities
 • Option  3  is  not  correct

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following is  not  a use of ultrasound?
options: A. Scanning a fetus during pregnancy
B. Non-destructive testing of materials such as to find leaks in copper pipes
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Broken bones are imaged using x-rays
 • The other options are all key uses of ultrasound waves

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement about a permanent bar magnet is  incorrect ?
options: A. The S-pole attracts the N-pole of another magnet
B. The S-pole repels the S-pole of another magnet
C. It cannot repel a non-magnetic material
D. It is made from a soft magnetic material (such as soft iron)
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The incorrect statement is  D  because:
 • A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field
 • This means it never loses its magnetism
 • Most permanent magnets are made from 'hard' iron, nickel, or cobalt
 • A soft magnetic material, such as soft iron, will only be magnetic whilst there is a current around it (such as in an electromagnet)
 • Once the current is switched off, it is demagnetised (loses its magnetism)
 • This means it wouldn't work as a permanent magnet
 A  is correct as opposite poles attract, so an S-pole will attract the N-pole of another magnet
 B  is correct as like poles repel, so an S-pole will repel the S-pole of another magnet
 C  is correct as permanent magnets can only attract or repel other magnetic materials, so it is true that they cannot repel non-magnetic materials

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A PVC (plastic) rod is rubbed with a nylon cloth. This process causes electrons to be transferred between the rod and the cloth, causing both objects to become charged.

 • If electrons move to the rod, the rod becomes negative
 • This means the two objects have  opposite  charges
 • Opposite charges  attract
 A  and  B  are incorrect as the charges will be opposite.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a mobile phone battery is 3.7 V. 
 What does this mean?
options: A. 3.7 J is the maximum energy the battery can provide in 1.0 s.
B. 3.7 J is the total energy the battery can provide before it has to be recharged.
C. 3.7 J of energy is provided by the battery to drive a charge of 1.0 C around a complete circuit.
D. 3.7 J of energy is provided by the battery to drive a current of 1.0 A around a complete circuit.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C because:
 • The e.m.f. is defined as the electrical work done by a source in moving a unit charge around a complete circuit
 • If the battery has an e.m.f. of 3.7 V, that means it takes 3.7 J to move 1.0 C of charge around a circuit
 A  is incorrect as this describes the power (energy transferred per second)
 B  is incorrect as this describes the total energy in the battery’s chemical energy store
 D  is incorrect as e.m.f. is the energy required to move charge, not current

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
An oven is wired into somebody’s kitchen. The oven is protected by a fuse, and functions normally, but the owner notices that the wires that connect the oven to the mains electricity supply get quite hot.
 What could be done to reduce the temperature of the wires?
options: Add a circuit breaker to the circuit.
B. Put thicker insulation on the wires.
C. Replace the wires with thicker diameter wires.
D. Replace the wires with thinner diameter wires.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The problem here is that the wires used to connect the oven are not rated for the amount of current the oven uses. This is an easy mistake to make, as ovens use more current than normal electrical devices.
 • Thicker diameter wires are required, since thicker wires have a smaller resistance, and therefore dissipate less heat when current flows through them. Remember:    gives the power dissipated by a component which has resistance.
 A  is incorrect as this would have no effect, as the oven is operating properly.
 B  is incorrect as thicker insulation might cause the wires to  feel  cooler, but they would still be just as hot. They would actually be less able to dissipate the heat they are generating, and are in greater danger of causing a fire.
 D  is incorrect as thinner wires would exacerbate the problem. They have a higher resistance, and would dissipate more heat, becoming even hotter.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, an e.m.f. is induced in the wire.
 Which of the following devices uses this effect?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, the induced e.m.f. can be used to drive a current
 • The combination of current and voltage can deliver electrical power to devices ( P  =  IV ), which causes them to work
 • This is the process used by a generator to produce electricity
 A  is incorrect as an electric motor works using the reverse effect: when a current is passed through a wire in a magnetic field, it experiences a force.
 C  is incorrect as a photon accelerator is a fictitious device, popularised on a children’s TV show in the early 90s called “Bucky O’Hare”. One might argue that a light bulb accelerates photons.
 D  is incorrect as a transformer uses the induction effect, but does not use a moving wire, it uses an alternating magnetic field to create the same effect.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
After electricity is generated at a power station, the voltage is increased significantly for transmission across the country via the national grid.
 What is the advantage of transmitting electricity at very high voltages?
options: A. It makes the electricity flow more quickly.
B. It increases the efficiency of the electricity transfer.
D. It is safer to transmit electricity at high voltage.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Since  P  =  IV , when the voltage increases, the current decreases
 • This is because the electrical power must be the same before and after transforming, otherwise, you create or destroy energy, which is not possible
 • The lower the current, the less power is dissipated as heat in the power lines
 • If less power is wasted, the transmission is more efficient
 A  is incorrect as electricity does not flow more or less quickly due to the voltage.
 C  is incorrect as power cannot be created or destroyed due to the conservation of energy. If the voltage goes up, the current comes down to compensate, since  P  =  IV.
 D  is incorrect as high voltage transmission is much  less  safe than low voltage transmission, but the rewards are worth the risk.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which device uses a split ring commutator?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because: 
 • a d.c. motor uses a split ring commutator to reverse the direction of the current through the coil every half turn, and, therefore, to keep it spinning in the same direction.
 • a.c. generators use slip rings, transformers have no moving parts, and relays use no rings at all.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 Steel is often known as a 'hard' magnetic material and iron as a 'soft' magnetic material due to the relative amount of time they remain magnetised.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Comets travel faster within the Solar System than they do when they are outside it.
 Which of the following gives the correct reason for this?
options: A comet near to the Sun has more gravitational potential energy.
B. Comets closer to the Sun transfer gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy due to conservation of energy.
C. A comet which is outside the Solar System has less energy than one which is passing through it.
D. Comets closer to the Sun transfer kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy due to conservation of energy.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Energy is always conserved

 • Gravitational potential energy  increases  when the comet is far from the Sun (and about to be pulled back towards it) and  decreases  when it is close to the Sun
 • The decrease in gravitational potential energy is balanced by an increase in kinetic energy

A student is timing the rate of cooling of a beaker of water. On a repeat run of the investigation, the student forgets to zero the stopwatch.
 The readings on the stopwatch at the start time and the end time are shown in Fig. 1.1
  Calculate how long it took the beaker to cool.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Cooling time = end time − start time
 • Firstly, consider the minutes
 • 23 − 11 = 12 minutes
 • Then consider the seconds
 • 27 − 19 = 8 seconds
 • Cooling time = 12 minutes and 8 seconds
 It is important to work out the minutes and the seconds separately, because if the number of seconds at the end time is greater than the number of seconds at the start time, you will need to adjust the number of minutes. 
 Remember that there are only 60 seconds in a minute, so time calculations can't be done easily with decimals. 
 Another method, would be to convert everything into seconds, do the calculation, and convert the answer into minutes.

 • Mass is the amount of matter in the cup, while weight is the strength of the gravitational force pulling that matter downwards.
 • As liquid leaves the cup, matter leaves the cup as evaporated vapour, and both the mass and weight decrease.
 A  is incorrect because the mass does not increase.
 B  is incorrect because neither the mass nor the weight increase.

An object with three forces acting on it is shown below.
  What is the resultant force acting on the object?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • To calculate the resultant force in this case you subtract all the upward forces from the downward force.
 • 200 - (75 + 35) = 90 N downwards.
 B  is incorrect as the downward forces have not been considered
 C  is incorrect as the upward forces have not been considered
 D  is incorrect as the direction is wrong

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A corkscrew is used to open a bottle of wine.
 Two forces are applied at each of the positions shown below.
  Which pair of forces produces the greatest turning force?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • We are looking for the corkscrew with the greatest moment.
 • In  D , both forces are acting in an anticlockwise direction about the pivot.
 • Both forces are the maximum distance away from the pivot (in the centre), which means the moment will be the maximum.
 A  is incorrect as the forces act in opposite directions (the topmost F is in the clockwise direction, the bottommost F is in the anticlockwise moment), so they cancel each other out.
 B  is incorrect as one of the forces is only halfway along the corkscrew handle and although both forces act in the anticlockwise direction about the pivot, because one of the moments is only halfway along the corkscrew, the combined moment in  B  is less than combined moments in corkscrew  D .
 C  is incorrect as the forces act in opposite directions about the pivot, and so cancel each other out, even though they are as far from the pivot as they can be.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: In which of the following situations would no resultant force be required?
options: A motorbike travelling round a bend at a constant speed.
B. A rocket accelerating straight upwards into space.
C. A ship sailing at a constant speed across the ocean.
D. A Formula One car accelerating off the starting grid.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Objects which travel at a constant speed in a straight line need no resultant force.
 • All the other objects are either changing speed, or direction, both of which require a resultant force.
 A  is incorrect as the motorbike is changing direction when going round a bend, this requires a resultant force.
 B  is incorrect as the rocket is accelerating, this requires a resultant force.
 D  is incorrect as the car is accelerating, this requires a resultant force.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A wooden block rests on a table.
  On which surface should the block be laid to produce the largest pressure on the table?
options: D. Any side, they will all produce the same pressure
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The equation pressure = force / area is used to determine pressure. Therefore we need the side with the smallest area to produce the largest pressure.
 • Multiplying the dimensions of all the sides leads us to the fact that side B has the smallest area, and, therefore, exerts the highest pressure.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as side A does not have the smallest area.
 D  is incorrect as the pressure depends on the area. It will not be the same on all sides because the area of each side is different.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows four measuring identical cylinders containing either distilled water or concentrated sugar solution.
 Which measuring cylinder has the least pressure at the base, due to the liquid?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Pressure in liquids is caused by two properties - the density and the depth of the liquid
 • Distilled water is less dense than a concentrated sugar solution since the sugar solution contains sugar molecules as well as water
 • Therefore for a given depth, there will be less pressure when distilled water is used
 • This eliminates both  C  and  D
 • Pressure increases with depth
 • Therefore the shallowest option from  A  and  B  is the correct answer
 • This is option  A

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A beaker of water, at its boiling point of 100  o C, is heated so that the liquid starts to become a gas, also at 100  o C.
 Which row of the table correctly compares the liquid phase with the gas phase under these conditions?
 |  
 | Average distance between the particles
 | Average speed of the particles
 |
 | A
 | the same in the liquid and the gas
 | the same in the liquid and the gas
 |
 | B
 | greater in the liquid
 | greater in the gas
 |
 | C
 | greater in the gas
 | greater in the liquid
 |
 | D
 | greater in the gas
 | the same in the liquid and the gas
 |
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D because:
 • The particles in a liquid are in contact with each other, while those in a gas are considerably further apart.
 • The average kinetic energy of each molecule is related to the temperature of the substance. This means that, if a substance has a higher temperature, its molecules will, on average, have a higher kinetic energy.
 • As Kinetic energy =    , the speed of the molecules will also be greater.
 • Since both the liquid water and the gaseous water are  both  at a temperature of 100  o C, their molecules both have  the same  kinetic energy, and are travelling at  the same  speed.
 Each of the other answers has made at least one error. Liquid particles are  always  closer together than gas particles.
 Most students incorrectly think that gas particles have a higher kinetic energy than liquid particles. This is  only  true   if the gas is also at a higher temperature than the liquid (which is usually, but not always, the case)

 Which of its properties decreases?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • As the iron cube is heated, it will expand.
 • This means its volume will  increase .
 • Its mass will stay the same, as no iron is being added or taken away.
 • Since    , the density will decrease.
 A  is incorrect as mass remains constant, as no iron is being added or taken away.
 C  is incorrect as volume  increases , it does not decrease.
 D  is incorrect as the block’s internal energy will  increase  as its temperature rises; it does not decrease.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 Identify the two properties.
options: C. Specific heat capacity and volume
D. State of matter and potential energy
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:

 • This is the internal energy of a substance

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A substance, which is initially in its solid form, is heated at a constant rate.
 The graph shows how its temperature changes with time.
  Between which points is the substance partly a liquid and partly a gas?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The substance will be partly liquid and partly gas during its boiling phase change.
 • The temperature of a substance does not change during a phase change, so these are shown by flat sections on the graph.
 • The first flat section will represent the melting phase change, so we are interested in the second flat section.
 A  is incorrect as this shows the solid rising in temperature.
 B  is incorrect as this shows the solid melting.
 C  is incorrect as this shows the liquid rising in temperature .

 Warm air rises because:
options: A. The air molecules expand and become less dense.
B. The air molecules move further apart, making the air less dense.
C. The air molecules contract, making the air less dense.
D. The air molecules move closer together, making the air less dense.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • As the temperature of air molecules increases, they move more quickly, and tend to be further apart, on average.
 • This makes the air less dense.
 • Less dense substances float on more dense substances.
 A  is incorrect as the molecules themselves remain exactly the same size and shape. They absolutely do  not  expand. This is a very common misconception among students.
 C  is incorrect as the air molecules do not contract, either.
 D  is incorrect as if the air molecules moved closer together, the density of the air would  increase .

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Two cars sit side by side, a black car and a white car. It is Summer.
  During the day both cars absorb infrared radiation from the Sun, and during the night, both cars lose energy by emitting infrared radiation.
 Which car heats up more quickly during the day, and which car cools down more quickly at night?
 |  
 | Car which heats up more quickly during the day
 | Car which cools down more quickly at night
 |
 | A
 | black
 | black
 |
 | B
 | black
 | white
 |
 | C
 | white
 | black
 |
 | D
 | white
 | white
 |
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Darker coloured objects emit  and  absorb infrared radiation at a greater rate than their light coloured counterparts.
 • A  greater rate of absorption  of infrared radiation raises the temperature more quickly.
 • A  greater rate of emission  of infrared radiation lowers the temperature more quickly.
 In general: black objects  change temperature  quickly, while white objects change temperature slowly.
 B  is incorrect as the white car will cool more slowly at night.
 C  is incorrect as the white car will heat up more slowly during the day.
 D  is incorrect as the white car will both heat up and cool more slowly than the black car.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which two points on the wave are exactly one wavelength apart?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • A wavelength is the distance between two identical points on a wave.
 • Q and S are identical points because they are both in the equilibrium position  and  the string is pointing in identical directions to their left and right, i.e. up on the left and down on the right.
 • A common mistake is to think Q and R are 1 wavelength apart because they are both on the equilibrium line. However, the string is pointing in opposite directions at each of these points.
 • There are plenty more ways to explain wavelength, like: to complete a wave you have to go up, down and back up again, but I rather like the first explanation.
 • It’s much easier to explain with a diagram:
  A  is incorrect as P and S are 1.25 wavelengths apart.
 B  is incorrect as Q and R are half a wavelength apart.
 D  is incorrect as P and R are 0.75 wavelengths apart.

The correct answer is  B  because:

 • All  electromagnetic  waves are  transverse .
 • Both infrared and red light waves are electromagnetic waves, so they are transverse.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: When light passes from a denser material into a less dense material
options: A. light slows down and bends toward the normal
B. light slows down and bends away from the normal
C. light speeds up and bends toward the normal
D. light speeds up and bends away from the normal
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:

 • It speeds up
 • It bends away from the normal

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because 
 the electromagnetic spectrum runs, in order of longest wavelength to shortest wavelength:
 • Radio waves
 • Microwaves
 • Infrared
 • Visible light
 • Ultra violet
 • X-Rays
 • Gamma (γ) rays 
 The table starts with the shortest EM wavelength (gamma rays) and runs to the longest EM wavelength (radio waves). That would make  D  microwaves. 
 A  is incorrect as this would be X-rays.

 C  is incorrect as this would be visible light.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used in remote controls?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D because:
 • Remote controls contain an infrared LED at the front. This is used to send coded signals to the TV that cannot be seen by the human eye.
 • It is possible, with certain mobile phone cameras, to see this infrared LED flashing when a button is pressed on a remote control. Give it a go. It won’t work with Apple phones as they include an IR filter over the lens of their cameras.
 A  is incorrect as microwaves are used for mobile phone and satellite communication, and for cooking in microwave ovens.
 B  is incorrect as visible light is used to see things.
 C  is incorrect as ultraviolet radiation is used to kill bacteria, to make security features in secure documents and banknotes glow and to make people’s clothes and teeth glow at nightclubs. Oh, it also gives you a suntan and causes skin cancer.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the lists below are metals that are ferrous?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Ferrous metals contain  iron
 • These are either iron itself or an alloy of iron, such as  steel
 • Therefore, steel and iron are both ferrous
 An alloy is a substance that contains more than one metal. Iron alloys all contain small amounts of iron. In the case of steel, this is iron and carbon.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student makes a series of statements about a permanent bar magnet.
 Which of them is true?
options: A. The North pole of a permanent bar magnet will repel the North pole of another magnet.
B. A permanent bar magnet must be made from a soft magnetic material.
C. A permanent bar magnet can repel a magnetic material.
D. The field lines of a permanent bar magnet cross each other where the field is strongest.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because North poles will repel North poles of other permanent magnets.
 B  is incorrect as soft magnetic materials lose their magnetism quickly. A permanent magnet would not be permanent if it were made from a soft magnetic material.
 C  is incorrect as magnetic materials become magnets when placed in a magnetic field. They always become magnetic in such a way as to  attract  the magnet that causes them to become magnetic. They would never repel.
 D  is incorrect as magnetic field lines  never  cross.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student rubs an acetate rod with a cloth, giving it a negative charge. She then holds it near an earthed, conducting sphere as shown in the diagrams below.
 Which diagram shows the correct distribution of charges on the conducting sphere?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The rod's negative charges  repel  the sphere's negatively charged electrons
 • The electrons move away from the surface,  along  the earth wire and  away  from the conducting sphere
 •  This leaves the conducting sphere with a net  positive  charge
 The other answers do not show the correct distribution of charge.
 Remember, the positive protons never move, the negative electrons are repelled by the negatively charged rod, causing them to move away from the protons.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the unit of electromotive force?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because: 
 • The unit of electromotive force (EMF) is the volt.
 A  is incorrect as the joule is the unit of energy.
 C  is incorrect as the ampere is the unit of current.
 D  is incorrect as the watt is the unit of power (there’s a great physics joke here, “Watt (what) is the unit of power?” to which the correct answer is “yes, it is”...!

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:

 • Rearranging  V = IR  gives   .
 • Substituting into the other equation gives:

 D  is incorrect as the voltage has incorrectly been multiplied by the resistance. This does not give anything useful.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the circuit diagrams above shows a fuse which has been correctly connected?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because: 
 • The fuse must be connected  in series  with the live wire, before any of the components in the circuit.
 A  is incorrect as if this fuse blew, the appliance would remain connected, the blowing of the fuse would have no effect on the safety of the circuit. In fact, this fuse would blow instantly every time it was connected because it short circuits the appliance.
 C  is incorrect as the appliance would still be live if this fuse blew, maintaining the risk of shock.
 D  is incorrect as if this fuse blew, it would not disconnect the circuit at all if the switch were closed.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A book shop owner sets up the circuit below, but they find that the lamp is too dim.
  What change can be made to the circuit to increase the brightness of the bulb?
options: A. Putting another resistor in parallel with the battery.
B. Putting a resistor in parallel with the bulb.
C. Putting another resistor in series with the resistor.
D. Putting another resistor in parallel with the resistor.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The brightness of the bulb depends on the power it dissipates,  P  =  IV , so any increase to the voltage or current in the part of the circuit containing the bulb (assuming the other does not change in the opposite direction) would increase its brightness.
 • Resistances in parallel are smaller than the smallest resistor in the combination. Adding another resistor in parallel with the original resistor would decrease the overall resistance of the circuit, and would increase the brightness of the bulb.
 A  is incorrect as this would not change the voltage across either the bulb or the resistor, and would not change the current through them. It would, however, give another branch for current to flow down, draining the battery more quickly.
 B  is incorrect as this would decrease the resistance of the bulb/new resistor combo, increasing the total current in the circuit (but not the current through the bulb), and decreasing the voltage across the bulb

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements about the current in ammeters  X ,  Y  and  Z  is correct?
options: A. The current through X equals the current through Y + the current through Z.
B. The current through X is equal to the current through Z.
C. The current through X is equal to the current through Y.
D. The current through Y is greater than the current through Z.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Observe that the two resistors are connected in  parallel
 • For resistors connected in parallel, the  current  before the resistors (X) is the sum of the current in each resistor
 • In other words, the current at Y  cannot  be greater than or equal to the current at X or Z
 • It should be clear that the current before and after the resistors must be the same
 A  is incorrect as X is equal to Z, so it cannot equal Y + Z
 C  is incorrect as the current splits as it enters the junction between the two resistors, therefore, some current must go to the lower resistor, meaning current X cannot equal current Y.
 D  is incorrect as the current through Y adds to the current through the bottom resistor, and gives current Z. Therefore Z cannot equal Y.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

 A  is incorrect as this would be true if the resistors were connected in series.
 B  and   C  are incorrect as this is not true.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: How many neutrons are in a nucleus of aluminium? The chemical symbol is given below:
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C because

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • If the initial count-rate is 300 counts per second, then the half-life is the time it takes for this to fall to half of it's starting level.
 • Half of 300 is 150 counts per second. This takes 40 seconds.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about  α -particles is correct?
options: A. α- particles consist of two protons and two electrons.
B. α- particles are the most penetrating type of radiation.
C. α- particles are a type of electromagnetic radiation.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • α -particles have a positive charge of +2 and an atomic mass of 4
 • This makes them heavier and more charged than other types of radiation
 • For this reason, they are more likely to interact with matter, causing  ionisation
 A  is incorrect as  α -particles consist of two protons and two neutrons. This means they have an overall charge of +2. They don’t contain any electrons.
 B  is incorrect as  γ -rays are the most penetrating.
 C  is incorrect as  γ -rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Identify the physical quantity that is  not  scalar.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Scalar quantities have magnitude only
 • Weight is a force
 • Forces have both magnitude and direction
 • Therefore, weight is a vector quantity
 Students commonly confuse weight and mass. 
 Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object, it has magnitude but no direction, therefore it is scalar.
 Weight is a force, it has magnitude and direction, therefore it is a vector quantity.

 Which calculation will give the correct average speed for the journey?

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph shows the journey undertaken by a car.
  Which equation correctly gives the distance travelled by the car?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The distance travelled by an object is given by the  area  under a speed-time graph
 • This is because distance = speed × time
 • The area in question is a triangle. The area of a triangle is calculated using ½ × base × height
 • Distance = area of triangle =  ½ × 6.5 × 8.0 = 26 m
 • Therefore equation  A  is correct
  B, C and D  are incorrect as these equations have been incorrectly set up.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The Moon orbits the Earth at a constant speed.
  Which of the arrows on the diagram shows the direction of the resultant force on the Moon?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • This is a circular motion problem
 • The resultant force always acts toward the centre of the circular path of an object
 • In the same direction as the acceleration
 • Option  D  is the only answer that points toward the centre

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A teacher has a hot cup of tea.
 Some of the liquid in the cup evaporates.
 Choose the line from the table below that correctly describes what happens to the mass and the weight of the tea in the cup.

 | increases

 | decreases

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Mass is the amount of matter in the cup, while weight is the strength of the gravitational force pulling that matter downwards.
 • As liquid leaves the cup, matter leaves the cup as evaporated vapour, and both the mass and weight decrease.
 A  is incorrect because the mass does not increase.
 B  is incorrect because neither the mass nor the weight increase.
 D  is incorrect because the weight does not increase.
