set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A corkscrew is used to open a bottle of wine.
 Two forces are applied at each of the positions shown below.
  Which pair of forces produces the greatest turning force?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • We are looking for the corkscrew with the greatest moment.
 • In  D , both forces are acting in an anticlockwise direction about the pivot.
 • Both forces are the maximum distance away from the pivot (in the centre), which means the moment will be the maximum.
 A  is incorrect as the forces act in opposite directions (the topmost F is in the clockwise direction, the bottommost F is in the anticlockwise moment), so they cancel each other out.
 B  is incorrect as one of the forces is only halfway along the corkscrew handle and although both forces act in the anticlockwise direction about the pivot, because one of the moments is only halfway along the corkscrew, the combined moment in  B  is less than combined moments in corkscrew  D .
 C  is incorrect as the forces act in opposite directions about the pivot, and so cancel each other out, even though they are as far from the pivot as they can be.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
In a classroom, a uniform beam with a pivot at its centre has a 15 N weight suspended from one end. An instrument fixed to the ceiling is attached to the same end.
  What instrument must be used to show that the resultant moment on a system in equilibrium is zero?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • The experiment to show that resultant moment is zero uses a newtonmeter - also called a force meter
 • To calculate the moment due to the instrument, the force of the instrument on the beam must be known - a force meter measures this force
 A ruler is also needed to measure the distance to determine the moment caused by the instrument, but the instrument itself needs to be able to measure force. A ruler would not be placed where the instrument is mentioned in the diagram.
 A similar experiment to this can be found in the revision notes.
 Make sure you know your scientific instruments - a momentmeter is not a real instrument - hopefully you spotted this!

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: A bullet is shot from a gun. The bullet moves forward and the gun moves in the opposite direction. Which of the following statements is true?
options: A. They move with the same velocity in opposite directions.
B. The bullet moves with a slower velocity due to its mass.
C. The total momentum of the system is zero.
D. The total momentum of the system does not stay constant before and after the collision.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The total momentum of the bullet and gun before shooting = the total momentum of the bullet and gun after shooting.
 • Before shooting the bullet and the gun are stationary so overall the total momentum will be zero.
 A  is incorrect as the velocities of the bullet and the gun will be different due to their different masses. However, they will move in opposite directions.
 B  is incorrect as the bullet will actually move faster due to having a smaller mass.
 D  is incorrect as the law of conservation of momentum states that momentum will always be constant before and after a collision.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A dummy is used in a crash test to investigate the safety of a new car. The deceleration of the dummy and the passenger compartment is measured.
  The deceleration of the dummy is less than the deceleration of the passenger compartment. 
 Why is this of benefit for the safety of the passenger?
options: A. Seat belts, crumple zones and airbags all absorb energy from the crash
B. The crash happens quickly so the passenger doesn’t feel anything
C. The force of impact on the passenger, and therefore harm, is reduced
D. The time over which the collision happens is elongated for the passenger
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The question is specifically asking why a shorter deceleration benefits the passenger.
 • Since F = ma, decreasing the value of  a  will subsequently decrease the force of the impact.
 A  is incorrect as although factually correct, this statement does not answer the question.
 B  is incorrect as a short collision time is the whole reason there is a large impact force since impulse = F x t, the shorter the collision time, the larger the impact force - the passenger will certainly always feel something!
 D  is incorrect as although factually correct, it does not answer the question

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows four measuring identical cylinders containing either distilled water or concentrated sugar solution.
 Which measuring cylinder has the least pressure at the base, due to the liquid?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Pressure in liquids is caused by two properties - the density and the depth of the liquid
 • Distilled water is less dense than a concentrated sugar solution since the sugar solution contains sugar molecules as well as water
 • Therefore for a given depth, there will be less pressure when distilled water is used

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Internal energy is affected by two properties of the particles which make up a substance. 
 Identify the two properties.
options: C. Specific heat capacity and volume
D. State of matter and potential energy
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The total energy stored inside a system is due to the particles that make up that system having motion and positions relative to each other

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following processes take place in a non-metal to allow the  conduction  of thermal energy?
 |  
 | Transfer of electrons
 | Lattice vibrations
 | Transfer of nuclei
 |
 | A
 | yes
 | yes
 | no
 |
 | B
 | no
 | yes
 | no
 |
 | C
 | yes
 | yes
 | yes
 |
 | D
 | no
 | yes
 | yes
 |
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Conduction  in  non-metals  happens because lattice  vibrations  are passed between neighbouring  atoms .
 • In metals, this process is assisted by free electrons being transferred between the lattice sites as well, but this question asks about  non-metals .
 • Nuclei do not move (in a translational way, they do vibrate) at all in solids, so nuclei are  never  transferred.
 A  is incorrect as electrons are only transferred in metals.
 C  is incorrect as nuclei are not transferred in the process of conduction. They do move in convection, though. Electrons are only transferred for conduction in metals.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A substance, which is initially in its solid form, is heated at a constant rate.
 The graph shows how its temperature changes with time.
  Between which points is the substance partly a liquid and partly a gas?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The substance will be partly liquid and partly gas during its boiling phase change.
 • The temperature of a substance does not change during a phase change, so these are shown by flat sections on the graph.
 • The first flat section will represent the melting phase change, so we are interested in the second flat section.
 A  is incorrect as this shows the solid rising in temperature.
 B  is incorrect as this shows the solid melting.
 C  is incorrect as this shows the liquid rising in temperature .

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following statements about convection is correct?
 Warm air rises because:
options: A. The air molecules expand and become less dense.
B. The air molecules move further apart, making the air less dense.
C. The air molecules contract, making the air less dense.
D. The air molecules move closer together, making the air less dense.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • As the temperature of air molecules increases, they move more quickly, and tend to be further apart, on average.
 • This makes the air less dense.
 • Less dense substances float on more dense substances.
 A  is incorrect as the molecules themselves remain exactly the same size and shape. They absolutely do  not  expand. This is a very common misconception among students.
 C  is incorrect as the air molecules do not contract, either.
 D  is incorrect as if the air molecules moved closer together, the density of the air would  increase .

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which two points on the wave are exactly one wavelength apart?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • A wavelength is the distance between two identical points on a wave.
 • Q and S are identical points because they are both in the equilibrium position  and  the string is pointing in identical directions to their left and right, i.e. up on the left and down on the right.
 • A common mistake is to think Q and R are 1 wavelength apart because they are both on the equilibrium line. However, the string is pointing in opposite directions at each of these points.
 • There are plenty more ways to explain wavelength, like: to complete a wave you have to go up, down and back up again, but I rather like the first explanation.
 • It’s much easier to explain with a diagram:
  A  is incorrect as P and S are 1.25 wavelengths apart.
 B  is incorrect as Q and R are half a wavelength apart.
 D  is incorrect as P and R are 0.75 wavelengths apart.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
When water waves travel from deeper water into more shallow water they are refracted.
  Why does the wave change direction in the manner shown?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because
 • Water waves travel more quickly on the surface of water when the water is deep compared to when it is shallow.
 • The change in speed causes the change in direction .
 A  is incorrect as the speed decreases, it does not increase.
 C  &  D  are incorrect as the frequency remains constant when a wave crosses a boundary.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: When light passes from a denser material into a less dense material
options: A. light slows down and bends toward the normal
B. light slows down and bends away from the normal
C. light speeds up and bends toward the normal
D. light speeds up and bends away from the normal
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • When light passes from a denser medium into a less dense medium
 • It speeds up
 • It bends away from the normal

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Below is a ray diagram showing the image formed by a thin, converging lens.
  Which of the following statements about the image is correct?
options: A. The image is virtual and can be seen by eye Y.
B. The image is inverted and can be seen by eye Y.
C. The image is real and can be seen by the eye at X.
D. The image is virtual and can be seen by eye X.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • We know the image is virtual because the light rays do not converge anywhere.
 • For an image to be real, light rays must converge, these diverge (get further apart).
 • The image is seen at a position which is a backward projection of the diverging light rays that pass through the lens.
 • No light gets to X, so the image cannot be seen there. An image can only be seen at a position that light actually reaches.
 • The dashed lines represent  projections  of the real light rays that pass through the lens, not actual light.
 B  is incorrect as the image is not inverted. Inverted means upside-down.
 C  is incorrect as the image is not real, since no light rays converge on its position.
 D  is incorrect as the image cannot be seen at X.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The table below shows the entire electromagnetic spectrum. It runs in order of increasing wavelength.
 Which region is microwaves?
 | γ-rays
 | A
 | B
 | C
 | infrared
 | D
 | radio waves
 |
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because 
 the electromagnetic spectrum runs, in order of longest wavelength to shortest wavelength:
 • Radio waves
 • Microwaves
 • Infrared
 • Visible light
 • Ultra violet
 • X-Rays
 • Gamma (γ) rays 
 The table starts with the shortest EM wavelength (gamma rays) and runs to the longest EM wavelength (radio waves). That would make  D  microwaves.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used in remote controls?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Remote controls contain an infrared LED at the front. This is used to send coded signals to the TV that cannot be seen by the human eye.
 • It is possible, with certain mobile phone cameras, to see this infrared LED flashing when a button is pressed on a remote control. Give it a go. It won’t work with Apple phones as they include an IR filter over the lens of their cameras.
 A  is incorrect as microwaves are used for mobile phone and satellite communication, and for cooking in microwave ovens.
 B  is incorrect as visible light is used to see things.
 C  is incorrect as ultraviolet radiation is used to kill bacteria, to make security features in secure documents and banknotes glow and to make people’s clothes and teeth glow at nightclubs. Oh, it also gives you a suntan and causes skin cancer.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student makes a series of statements about a permanent bar magnet.
 Which of them is true?
options: A. The North pole of a permanent bar magnet will repel the North pole of another magnet.
B. A permanent bar magnet must be made from a soft magnetic material.
C. A permanent bar magnet can repel a magnetic material.
D. The field lines of a permanent bar magnet cross each other where the field is strongest.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because North poles will repel North poles of other permanent magnets.
 B  is incorrect as soft magnetic materials lose their magnetism quickly. A permanent magnet would not be permanent if it were made from a soft magnetic material.
 C  is incorrect as magnetic materials become magnets when placed in a magnetic field. They always become magnetic in such a way as to  attract  the magnet that causes them to become magnetic. They would never repel.
 D  is incorrect as magnetic field lines  never  cross.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which diagram shows the correct electric field pattern between two oppositely charged parallel plates?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Electric field lines always go from positive (+) to negative (-)
 • Between parallel plates, the field lines are  parallel  and  equally spaced
 • This pattern is shown by  B
 A  and  C  are incorrect as electric field lines do not run parallel to the plates.
 D  is incorrect as the field lines are running in the wrong direction, - to +

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the correct unit of charge?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • The unit of charge is the  coulomb  (C)
 A  is incorrect as the ampere (A) is the unit of current
 C  is incorrect as the newton (N) is the unit of force
 D  is incorrect as the volt (V) is the unit of potential difference

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student considers how changing the diameter and length of a wire affects its resistance.
 Which row shows the changes that could be made to the length and diameter of the wire to  decrease  its resistance?
 |  
 | Change to length
 | Change to diameter
 |
 | A
 | increase
 | increase
 |
 | B
 | increase
 | decrease
 |
 | C
 | decrease
 | increase
 |
 | D
 | decrease
 | decrease
 |
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The resistance of a wire is  directly   proportional  to its  length
 • Therefore, a  shorter  wire would give a lower resistance
 • The resistance of a wire is  inversely   proportional  to its  diameter
 • Therefore, a  larger  diameter wire would give a lower resistance
 A  is incorrect as increasing the length would increase the resistance of the wire.
 B  is incorrect as both of these factors would increase the resistance of the wire.
 D  is incorrect as decreasing the diameter would increase the resistance of the wire.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A homeowner buys a security light that switches on automatically when it gets dark.
 The security light contains the circuit, shown below.
  When it gets dark, what happens to the resistance of the LDR, and what happens to the potential difference across the LDR?
 |  
 | Resistance of LDR
 | p.d. across LDR
 |
 | A
 | increases
 | increases
 |
 | B
 | decreases
 | increases
 |
 | C
 | increases
 | decreases
 |
 | D
 | decreases
 | decreases
 |
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Remember that in LDRs that the resistance  increases  as the light intensity  decreases  (it gets dark). 
 • Recognise the diagram as the layout for a potential divider.
 • Potential   dividers  divide up the voltage within a circuit so that parts of a circuit only receive a  specific  voltage. Potential dividers usually consist of two or more resistors arranged in series across a power supply.
 • As the resistance in the LDR increases in relation to the other resistor (which has a fixed resistance), it causes the potential difference across the LDR to increase.
 B  is incorrect as the resistance of an LDR  increases  as light level decreases.
 C  is incorrect as the p.d. across a component in a potential divider circuit will be higher across the higher resistance.
 D  is incorrect as the resistance of an LDR  increases  as light level decreases.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following statements about the current in ammeters  X ,  Y  and  Z  is correct?
options: A. The current through X equals the current through Y + the current through Z.
B. The current through X is equal to the current through Z.
C. The current through X is equal to the current through Y.
D. The current through Y is greater than the current through Z.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Observe that the two resistors are connected in  parallel
 • For resistors connected in parallel, the  current  before the resistors (X) is the sum of the current in each resistor
 • In other words, the current at Y  cannot  be greater than or equal to the current at X or Z
 • It should be clear that the current before and after the resistors must be the same
 A  is incorrect as X is equal to Z, so it cannot equal Y + Z
 C  is incorrect as the current splits as it enters the junction between the two resistors, therefore, some current must go to the lower resistor, meaning current X cannot equal current Y.
 D  is incorrect as the current through Y adds to the current through the bottom resistor, and gives current Z. Therefore Z cannot equal Y.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
All the light bulbs in the diagrams above are identical. Each one is rated as ‘10 W, 230 V’.
 In which of the diagrams are all the bulbs working at their normal brightness?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • All the bulbs are connected in  parallel , and so will have the same potential difference across them.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A magnetic field can be represented by the diagram shown below. The dots represent magnetic field lines coming out of the page.
  A beam of alpha particles is directed through the field as shown above. Alpha particles, being charged, will be deflected by the field.
 In which direction will the alpha particles be deflected?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Using Fleming's left-hand rule:
 • the field (first finger) is directed out of the page
 • the current (second finger) is directed in the direction of the alpha particle beam since they are positively charged
 • the force (thumb) will be pointing downwards
 • Therefore, the alpha particle is deflected  downwards

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement about  α -particles is correct?
options: A. α- particles consist of two protons and two electrons.
B. α- particles are the most penetrating type of radiation.
C. α- particles are a type of electromagnetic radiation.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • α -particles have a positive charge of +2 and an atomic mass of 4
 • This makes them heavier and more charged than other types of radiation
 • For this reason, they are more likely to interact with matter, causing  ionisation
 A  is incorrect as  α -particles consist of two protons and two neutrons. This means they have an overall charge of +2. They don’t contain any electrons.
 B  is incorrect as  γ -rays are the most penetrating.
 C  is incorrect as  γ -rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation.

 • F × 0.50 = 1.5 N

 • We, therefore, require six 0.5 N weights to balance the yardarm.

 | increases
 | decreases
 |
 | C
 | decreases
 | increases
 |
 | D
 | decreases
 | decreases
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The average kinetic energy of the molecules in a substance is proportional to the temperature of the substance. So as the temperature in the bottle rises, the average kinetic energy per molecule will also increase.
 • Since  KE =   , increasing the kinetic energy also increases the speed of the air molecules.
 • Pressure against the inside walls of the container is caused by the air molecules colliding with the walls.
 • The faster the molecules are moving, the greater the force they apply when they collide with the container.
 • As the volume of the container remains constant, the area over which this force is exerted remains constant.
 • Remember  
 • Since the air molecules are moving faster, they exert more pressure on the walls of the container.
 The other answers have one or both of the statements incorrect, for the reasons outlined above.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Air is trapped inside a cylinder. The volume of the cylinder cannot change.
 The temperature of the air is increased.
 Which of the graphs below shows the correct relationship between pressure and temperature?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • As the temperature of a gas, in a container with a constant volume, is increased, its pressure will increase.
 • This is because higher temperature gas molecules move faster, hit the walls of the container harder, and exert more force on them, and pressure = force / area.
 • Graph C shows a linear increase of pressure with temperature.
 A  is incorrect as this graph shows pressure reducing at a linear rate with temperature. This, also, is not true.
 B  is incorrect as this graph shows that pressure remains constant. We know this not to be true.
 D  is incorrect as this graph shows an inverse relationship between pressure and temperature. This would be the correct answer if the question were about the relationship between pressure and  volume .

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement best describes a metal experiencing thermal expansion?
options: A. The size of the metal atoms increases
B. The space between the metal atoms increases
C. The metal atoms change state
D. The metal atoms gain enough energy to overcome the intermolecular forces of attraction holding them in place
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Expansion happens because the atoms gain energy and move faster
 • Therefore, the space between the atoms increases
 It is a common misconception that the size of the atoms / molecules / particles increases with expansion. This is not true! As the particles move more and more with the gain in energy, the space between the particles increases. This is true for a solid, a liquid, and a gas.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows four water molecules in a swimming pool. It also shows how much energy each molecule has.
 Which of the water molecules is most likely to  evaporate  from the liquid?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Evaporation happens to molecules which:
 • Have a high energy
 • Are at the surface of a liquid.
 • Molecule B fulfils both of these criteria.
 A  is incorrect as although this molecule is moving quickly, it is nowhere near the surface. It might have the energy to escape, but it has nowhere to escape  to .
 C  is incorrect as whilst this molecule is at the surface of the pool, its energy is not high enough to escape; it simply isn't moving fast enough.
 D  is incorrect as this molecule has nowhere to escape to, and it doesn’t have the energy to move fast either.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
In modern housing, it is convenient to locate heaters so they are not on the walls, taking up valuable wall space for furniture.
 Other than wall-mounted radiators, two other options would be viable: ceiling heaters or underfloor heaters.
  Which of the two options would heat the room more effectively and why?
 |  
 | Option
 | Explanation
 |
 | A
 | ceiling-mounted
 | hot air is more dense and falls
 |
 | B
 | ceiling-mounted
 | hot air is less dense and falls
 |
 | C
 | underfloor
 | hot air is less dense and rises
 |
 | D
 | underfloor
 | hot air is more dense and rises
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The fact that hotter air is less dense, and so it rises, is what makes underfloor heating the best.
 • Heat given off from underfloor heating will rise to the ceiling, and heat the whole room on the way up.
 • If the heater were in the ceiling, on the other hand, all the warm air would be created at the ceiling, and would stay there, leaving the floor rather cold.
 • It's also nice on your toes!
 Ceiling-mounted heaters  are  a thing, but you tend to need a fan with them to blow the hot air back down to the ground. Or at least really, really good air circulation.
 A  is incorrect as hot air is less dense, not more dense.
 B  is incorrect as hot air is less dense, but it does not fall
 D  is incorrect as hot air is less dense, not more dense.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student suggests some uses for the knowledge that black and white objects emit and absorb different amounts of infrared radiation.
 Which of her suggestions is correct?
options: A. Coffee mugs should be black to keep the coffee hot.
B. Houses in hot countries should be painted white to keep the occupants cool.
C. White clothing will help you cool down much faster.
D. Solar heating panels should be white to heat the water more quickly.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Black coloured objects emit  and  absorb infrared radiation at a greater rate than white objects.
 • The only correct statement is B, white houses in the hot countries would absorb infrared more slowly than black ones, so they would keep their occupants cool.
 A  is incorrect as a black coffee mug would emit IR more quickly, cooling the coffee faster.
 C  is incorrect as white clothing would emit IR more slowly, keeping you warmer for longer.
 D  is incorrect as white solar heating panels would absorb IR more slowly, heating the water more slowly.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the unit of wave speed?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Wave speed is a measure of how much distance a wave crosses per second.
 • The units are, therefore, of distance / time, or metres / seconds, metres per second.
 A  is incorrect as this is the unit of frequency.
 B  is incorrect as this is the unit of wavelength, and sometimes amplitude as well.
 C  is incorrect as this is the unit of time period.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Water waves travel from deeper water to more shallow water. This causes them to refract.
 Which wave property always remains the same when refraction occurs?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Every wavefront that hits the boundary has to leave the boundary.
 • Since frequency is defined as the number of waves (or wavefronts) that pass a point per second, this has to be the same on both sides of the boundary.
 • Anything else can change.
 A  is incorrect as wavelength changes when a wave refracts.
 C  is incorrect as amplitude can change when a wave refracts, especially if the water's depth changes.
 D  is incorrect as by definition, speed changes when a wave refracts.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An object is placed in front of a mirror. Where is the image formed, and is the image real or virtual?

 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
  • The ray diagram demonstrates how the image is formed.
 • Where the projected rays cross, is where a virtual image is formed.
 • Virtual images are formed by projected rays, while real images are formed by the convergence of actual light rays.
 • Plane mirrors always form virtual images.
 Y  is the location at which the eye would be positioned in order to see the image clearly.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows a ray of light being totally internally reflected at the boundary between substances A and B.
  Which row in the table must be true?
 |  
 | Angle of incidence
 | Substance A
 |
 | A
 | greater than critical angle
 | greater refractive index than B
 |
 | B

 | smaller refractive index than B
 |
 | C
 | less than critical angle
 | greater refractive index than B
 |
 | D
 | less than critical angle
 | smaller refractive index than B
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • This question is about total internal reflection.
 • If the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle, the light will be totally internally reflected.
 • Total internal reflection only works when the substance the light is going from has a higher refractive index than the substance it is going to, from glass to air for example.
 B  is incorrect as substance A must have a greater refractive index than substance B.
 C and D  are incorrect as the angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: In what way are microwaves different from ultraviolet waves?
options: A. Ultraviolet waves travel faster than microwaves in a vacuum.
B. Microwaves have a longer wavelength than ultraviolet waves.
C. Microwaves have a higher frequency than ultraviolet waves.
D. Microwaves are longitudinal while ultraviolet waves are transverse.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B because
 • The electromagnetic spectrum contains the following types of waves in the order you have probably learned them. This is in order of  increasing   frequency  and  decreasing   wavelength
 • Radio waves
 • Microwaves
 • Infrared
 • Visible light
 • Ultra violet
 • X-Rays
 • Gamma rays 
 • We can see that  ultraviolet  waves have both a  higher   frequency  and a  smaller   wavelength  than  microwaves .
 • Therefore, the only correct answer is B
 A  is incorrect as  all  electromagnetic waves travel at  the same  speed in a vacuum.
 C  is incorrect as microwaves have a  lower  frequency than ultraviolet.
 D  is incorrect as both microwaves and ultraviolet are transverse waves.  All  electromagnetic waves are transverse.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The table gives common uses of electromagnetic radiation.
 Which row correctly matches the type of electromagnetic radiation with its use?
 |  
 | Detecting banknote forgery
 | TV remote controllers
 | Sterilising medical instruments
 |
 | A
 | microwaves
 | visible light
 | microwaves
 |
 | B
 | infrared
 | infrared
 | γ-rays
 |
 | C
 | ultraviolet
 | radio waves
 | infrared
 |
 | D
 | ultraviolet
 | infrared
 | γ-rays
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Ultraviolet  light causes a phenomenon called  luminescence . This makes special inks glow when they are exposed to ultraviolet light. This special ink is difficult to forge.
 • TV  remote controllers send signals to the TV using an  infrared  LED built into the front of the controller (usually).
 • Sealed  medical   instruments  are sterilised using  γ-rays  at the factory before they are sent out to medical practices and hospitals. γ-rays kill all the bacteria and viruses that might be on the instrument.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following choices of metal would be suitable for:
 • Use as a permanent magnet?
 • Use as the core in an electromagnet?
 |  
 | Use as a permanent magnet

 |

 |

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • A hard magnetic material is required for a permanent magnet. Steel is a hard magnetic material that will retain its magnetism for a long time.
 • A soft magnetic material is required for the core of an electromagnet. A material that loses its magnetism quickly is needed, so that the electromagnet can ‘let go’ of whatever it is holding.
 The other answers do not pair iron with the core of an electromagnet, and/or steel with the permanent magnet.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which pair of quantities have the same units?
options: C. Electromotive force and potential difference
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The units of electromotive force and potential difference both have the units of  volts
 Current is measured in  amps (A) , and resistance is measured in  ohms (Ω) .

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student wants to charge up some rods by rubbing them with a cloth made from a suitable material.
 He has a number of rods to choose from: a copper rod, a PVC rod, an aluminium rod and a glass rod.
 Which two of the rods would hold a charge when rubbed with an appropriate cloth?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Electrical conductors cannot hold a charge when rubbed by a cloth, as electrons very quickly flow into (or out of) them from whatever is touching them.
 • Therefore, only  electrical   insulators  can be  charged  by  rubbing . Glass and PVC are electrical insulators. Aluminium and copper are not.
 A  is incorrect as aluminium is an electrical conductor.
 B  is incorrect as copper is an electrical conductor.
 C  is incorrect as both aluminium and copper are electrical conductors.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The circuit diagram shows cells connected with a resistor in a series circuit. 
 Each cell has an electromotive force (e.m.f.) of 1.5 V
  What is the total e.m.f. in the circuit?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D because:
 • There are 7 cells with e.m.f. of 1.6 V
 • All cells point in the same direction, so the total e.m.f. is equal to the sum of their individual e.m.f.s
 • Total e.m.f. = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 V
 A  is incorrect as this is the e.m.f. of a single cell
 B  is incorrect as this is the e.m.f. of the battery on the right
 C  is incorrect as this is the e.m.f. of the battery at the top

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The plug for an electric lamp contains a 3 A fuse. The fuse’s job is to protect the lamp if too much current flows.
 Where is the fuse positioned, and what happens when the fuse does its job?
 |  
 | Where is it positioned?
 | What does it do?
 |
 | A
 | live wire
 | reduces the current to 3 A
 |
 | B
 | neutral wire
 | breaks the circuit
 |
 | C
 | live wire
 | breaks the circuit
 |
 | D
 | neutral wire
 | reduces the current to 3 A
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The live wire is the one down which the push and pull from the power source comes. Putting the fuse on this wire means that, if it blows, there will be no power delivered to the circuit.
 • When a fuse does its job, a small wire inside the fuse melts. This breaks the circuit, meaning no current can flow through the device.
 A  is incorrect as a fuse is not capable of reducing the current in a circuit. It can only break the circuit if too much current flows.
 B  is incorrect as the fuse must be positioned on the live wire, otherwise there is a risk of shock if somebody touches a damaged appliance.
 D  is incorrect as a fuse is not capable of reducing the current in a circuit. It can only break the circuit if too much current flows.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A homeowner buys a security light that switches on automatically when it gets dark.
 The security light contains the circuit, shown below.
  When it gets dark, what happens to the resistance of the LDR, and what happens to the potential difference across the LDR?
 |  
 | Resistance of LDR
 | p.d. across LDR
 |

 | increases
 | increases
 |
 | B
 | decreases
 | increases
 |
 | C
 | increases
 | decreases
 |
 | D
 | decreases
 | decreases
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Remember that in LDRs that the resistance  increases  as the light intensity  decreases  (it gets dark). 
 • Recognise the diagram as the layout for a potential divider.
 • Potential   dividers  divide up the voltage within a circuit so that parts of a circuit only receive a  specific  voltage. Potential dividers usually consist of two or more resistors arranged in series across a power supply.
 • As the resistance in the LDR increases in relation to the other resistor (which has a fixed resistance), it causes the potential difference across the LDR to increase.
 B  is incorrect as the resistance of an LDR  increases  as light level decreases.
 C  is incorrect as the p.d. across a component in a potential divider circuit will be higher across the higher resistance.
 D  is incorrect as the resistance of an LDR  increases  as light level decreases.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student connects together some identical resistors in three different combinations, as shown in the diagram.
 Which of the answers below shows the correct order of the combinations from the lowest resistance to the highest?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Resistances in parallel are smaller than the smallest resistor in the combination
 • This means that combination  Q  has the smallest resistance
 • Resistances in series add up, so, the more resistors in series with each other, the higher the resistance
 • Therefore,  P  has the largest resistance, and  R  has the second-largest resistance
 • Hence, from lowest to highest resistance:  Q  →  R  →  P
 A  is incorrect as this is not the correct order.
 B  is incorrect as this order spells the name of a well-known football club, but it does not give the correct order of resistances.
 D  is incorrect as this order is the reverse of the correct answer.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which diagram correctly shows the magnetic field lines around a current-carrying wire if the current is directed out of the page?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 Which of the following statements represents a step-up transformer?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary coil than on the primary coil
 • This means that N s  > N p  (or N p  < N s )

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement is  not  a method used to minimise the risk caused by working with radioactive sources.
options: A. Store the sources in lead-lined boxes.
B. Minimise the amount of time spent handling the sources.
D. Keep the source as far away as possible, for example, using a pair of tongs.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The temperature  does not  change the radioactivity of the source.
 • Shielding the source with lead, reducing the time spent handling the source and keeping as far away from the source as feasible are all effective ways of reducing the risk from radiation.

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A skydiver is falling at terminal velocity. He has not yet opened his parachute.
 He opens his parachute.

 |  
 | Direction of the skydiver’s velocity
 | Direction of the skydiver’s acceleration
 |
 | A
 | upwards
 | upwards
 |
 | B
 | upwards
 | downwards
 |
 | C
 | downwards
 | upwards
 |
 | D
 | downwards
 | downwards

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The skydiver continues to fall downwards.
 • The parachute creates a very large force of air resistance when it is opened.
 • This air resistance force is much larger than the skydiver’s weight (force downward) and so the resultant force is upward.
 • Since Force = mass x acceleration, the acceleration is also upwards.
 • This has the effect of slowing the skydiver down,  not  causing them to move upwards.
 A  is incorrect as the skydiver does not move upwards.
 B  is incorrect as the skydiver does not move upwards
 D  is incorrect as if the skydiver accelerated downwards, he would speed up.

 B  is incorrect as the longer beam will weigh more because there is more of it.
 C  is incorrect as the longer beam will have a greater mass because there is more of it.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
In an experiment to determine the nature of liquids, some very tiny pollen grains are suspended in water. They are illuminated by a bright light, and observed under a microscope.
  The view through the microscope is of small, bright dots, which move about at random, rapidly and they frequently change direction.
 Which of the following would be the correct explanation for the observation through the microscope?
options: A. The bright dots are water molecules, being hit by other water molecules.
B. The bright dots are water molecules, which are vibrating due to their thermal kinetic energy.
C. The bright dots are pollen grains, which are being hit many times per second by water molecules.
D. The bright dots are pollen grains, which are vibrating due to their thermal kinetic energy.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • This random motion of pollen grains is called  Brownian   motion .
 • Pollen grains are constantly being buffeted around by tiny water molecules, which are too small to see with a microscope.
 • This is what causes their  random  motion.
 A  is incorrect as water molecules are too small to be seen with a microscope.
 B  is incorrect as water molecules are too small to be seen with a microscope. They  are  thermally moving, but this motion cannot be seen.
 D  is incorrect as the molecules that make up the pollen grains are vibrating due to their thermal energy, but this does not make the  entire  pollen grain vibrate. The thermal vibrations are random, and cancel out, on average.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement best describes a metal experiencing thermal expansion?
options: A. The size of the metal atoms increases
B. The space between the metal atoms increases
C. The metal atoms change state
D. The metal atoms gain enough energy to overcome the intermolecular forces of attraction holding them in place
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Expansion happens because the atoms gain energy and move faster
 • Therefore, the space between the atoms increases
 It is a common misconception that the size of the atoms / molecules / particles increases with expansion. This is not true! As the particles move more and more with the gain in energy, the space between the particles increases. This is true for a solid, a liquid, and a gas.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Two beakers, X and Y, containing different liquids are heated by a student.
 Both beakers contain the same mass of liquid, and are heated using the same heater set to the same power.
 The graph shows how the temperature of each liquid changes with time.
  What conclusion can be correctly drawn from the graph?
options: A. X has a higher melting point than Y.
B. Y boils sooner than X.
C. X has a lower specific heat capacity than Y.
D. Y has a higher boiling point than X.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1℃.
 • 
 • If energy is supplied at the same rate to equal masses of liquid, then the one with the lower specific heat capacity will show the greater temperature change, as it requires less energy to increase its temperature by 1℃
 • This means that the substance with the steeper gradient on the graph will have the lower specific heat capacity.
 • Therefore X has a lower specific heat capacity than Y.
 A  is incorrect as we have no information about the melting point of either substance.
 B  is incorrect as X actually boils sooner than Y.
 D  is incorrect as X has the higher boiling point.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows four water molecules in a swimming pool. It also shows how much energy each molecule has.
 Which of the water molecules is most likely to  evaporate  from the liquid?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Evaporation happens to molecules which:
 • Have a high energy
 • Are at the surface of a liquid.
 • Molecule B fulfils both of these criteria.
 A  is incorrect as although this molecule is moving quickly, it is nowhere near the surface. It might have the energy to escape, but it has nowhere to escape  to .
 C  is incorrect as whilst this molecule is at the surface of the pool, its energy is not high enough to escape; it simply isn't moving fast enough.
 D  is incorrect as this molecule has nowhere to escape to, and it doesn’t have the energy to move fast either.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The walls of a vacuum flask contain two layers of glass, separated by a vacuum.
  Which method(s) of thermal energy transfer are prevented by the vacuum?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The vacuum is helpful because it contains no particles at all.
 • This means that the methods of  thermal  energy transfer that involve  particles :  conduction  and  convection , cannot take place in a vacuum.
 A  is incorrect as radiation can still travel through a vacuum.
 B  is incorrect as radiation can still travel through a vacuum, though conduction is prevented.
 C  is incorrect as it  does  prevent convection, but radiation can still travel through the vacuum.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
In modern housing, it is convenient to locate heaters so they are not on the walls, taking up valuable wall space for furniture.
 Other than wall-mounted radiators, two other options would be viable: ceiling heaters or underfloor heaters.
  Which of the two options would heat the room more effectively and why?
 |  
 | Option
 | Explanation
 |
 | A
 | ceiling-mounted
 | hot air is more dense and falls
 |
 | B
 | ceiling-mounted
 | hot air is less dense and falls
 |
 | C
 | underfloor
 | hot air is less dense and rises
 |
 | D
 | underfloor
 | hot air is more dense and rises
 |
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The fact that hotter air is less dense, and so it rises, is what makes underfloor heating the best.
 • Heat given off from underfloor heating will rise to the ceiling, and heat the whole room on the way up.
 • If the heater were in the ceiling, on the other hand, all the warm air would be created at the ceiling, and would stay there, leaving the floor rather cold.
 • It's also nice on your toes!
 Ceiling-mounted heaters  are  a thing, but you tend to need a fan with them to blow the hot air back down to the ground. Or at least really, really good air circulation.
 A  is incorrect as hot air is less dense, not more dense.
 B  is incorrect as hot air is less dense, but it does not fall
 D  is incorrect as hot air is less dense, not more dense.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the unit of wave speed?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Wave speed is a measure of how much distance a wave crosses per second.
 • The units are, therefore, of distance / time, or metres / seconds, metres per second.
 A  is incorrect as this is the unit of frequency.
 B  is incorrect as this is the unit of wavelength, and sometimes amplitude as well.
 C  is incorrect as this is the unit of time period.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Water waves travel from deeper water to more shallow water. This causes them to refract.
 Which wave property always remains the same when refraction occurs?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Every wavefront that hits the boundary has to leave the boundary.
 • Since frequency is defined as the number of waves (or wavefronts) that pass a point per second, this has to be the same on both sides of the boundary.
 • Anything else can change.
 A  is incorrect as wavelength changes when a wave refracts.
 C  is incorrect as amplitude can change when a wave refracts, especially if the water's depth changes.
 D  is incorrect as by definition, speed changes when a wave refracts.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Resistances in parallel are smaller than the smallest resistor in the combination
 • This means that combination  Q  has the smallest resistance
 • Resistances in series add up, so, the more resistors in series with each other, the higher the resistance
 • Therefore,  P  has the largest resistance, and  R  has the second-largest resistance
 • Hence, from lowest to highest resistance:  Q  →  R  →  P
 A  is incorrect as this is not the correct order.
 B  is incorrect as this order spells the name of a well-known football club, but it does not give the correct order of resistances.
 D  is incorrect as this order is the reverse of the correct answer.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Realise that this question concerns electromagnetic induction
 • You can disregard answers  A  and  D . The poles induced in the solenoid will change as the direction of the magnet changes
 • When the north pole of the magnet is moved towards the left-hand end of the coil, the induced current flows anticlockwise.

 • Hence answer C is correct

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: When a substance is heated and its temperature rises, which statement about its particles is correct?
options: A. The particles become fixed in position.
B. The mass of the particles increases.
C. The average kinetic energy of the particles increases.
D. The particles move further apart.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles within a substance
 • When a substance is heated, energy is transferred to its particles, causing them to move (or vibrate) faster
 • This increase in particle motion directly corresponds to an increase in their average kinetic energy, which is observed as a rise in temperature
 A  is incorrect as particles become fixed in position during solidification or freezing, which is a change of state usually caused by a drop in temperature.
 B  is incorrect as the mass of individual particles is a fundamental property and does not change with temperature.
 D  is incorrect as particles typically move further apart when a substance expands due to heating, but this is a consequence of increased kinetic energy and intermolecular forces, not what temperature itself measures or what always happens (e.g., if heated at constant volume).

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • Direct current (d.c.) is a flow of charge that travels in one direction only, meaning the voltage remains on one side of the zero line (usually constant)
 • Alternating current (a.c.) is a flow of charge that continuously reverses its direction, which is shown on a graph by the voltage moving between positive and negative values
 • Supply X shows a constant positive value, identifying it as d.c.
 • Supply Y shows a wave that crosses the zero line, identifying it as a.c.
 A  is incorrect as it reverses the identification of both graphs.

 When interpreting voltage–time graphs, remember that d.c. stays on one side of the zero line (constant polarity), while a.c. crosses the zero line repeatedly (changing polarity). A quick way to identify a.c. is to look for a waveform that oscillates above and below zero.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

 • Redshift occurs when the light observed from an object has a longer wavelength than the light originally emitted

 • Observations of redshift from almost all distant galaxies show that they are moving away from us
 • This provides evidence that the Universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang Theory
 B  is incorrect because moving towards the Earth would cause a decrease in wavelength (blueshift).
 C  is incorrect as the speed of light in a vacuum is a constant and the galaxies are known to be in motion.
 D  is incorrect as the expansion of the Universe happens in all directions and does not imply that the Earth is in a special central position.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A skydiver falls before opening her parachute. 
  Which graph correctly shows how her speed changes with time?
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is B
 • At the start of the fall, the only downward force is weight, so the skydiver accelerates rapidly.
 • As speed increases, air resistance increases
 • The resultant downward force decreases, so the acceleration decreases
 • The curve, therefore, rises with a decreasing gradient
 • Eventually, air resistance equals weight, the resultant force is zero, and speed stays constant — this is terminal velocity
 • The curve levels off
 A  is incorrect because a straight line means constant acceleration throughout, which would only happen if there were no air resistance.
 C  is incorrect because the skydiver starts from rest and speeds up during free fall — speed does not decrease.
 D  is incorrect because speed does not peak and then fall before the parachute opens. A decrease in speed would only occur after the parachute opens (which is not shown in this question).

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
An aeroplane flies horizontally at constant speed as shown.
  Which statement about the resultant force on the aeroplane is correct?
options: A. There is no resultant force on the aeroplane.
B. There is a resultant force on the aeroplane in the direction of travel.
C. There is a resultant force on the aeroplane in the opposite direction to the direction of travel.
D. There is a resultant force on the aeroplane vertically downwards.
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is A
 • An object moving at a  constant speed  in a straight line has zero acceleration
 • Newton’s first law states that an object will continue to move at a constant velocity unless acted upon by a resultant force
 • Since the aeroplane is moving at a constant speed, and its direction is not changing, the horizontal forces (thrust and drag) and vertical forces (lift and weight) must be  balanced
 • Therefore, the resultant force on the aeroplane is zero
 B  is incorrect as a resultant force in the direction of travel would cause the aeroplane to accelerate and increase its speed.
 C  is incorrect as a resultant force in the opposite direction to travel would act as a braking force and cause the aeroplane to decelerate.
 D  is incorrect as a resultant force acting vertically downwards would cause the aeroplane to accelerate towards the Earth and change its vertical height.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph shows the load-extension graph for a spring.
  What does point P represent?
options: A. the maximum load the spring can withstand
B. the limit of proportionality of the spring
C. the maximum extension of the spring
D. the spring constant of the spring
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is B
 • Point P is where the straight-line section of the graph ends and the line begins to curve
 • This is the  limit of proportionality : the point beyond which the extension is no longer directly proportional to the applied force
 • Below point P, the graph is a straight line through the origin, meaning force and extension are directly proportional (Hooke's law applies)
 A  &  C  are incorrect because the maximum load and the maximum extension would be at the far right end of the graph, not where the curve begins.
 D  is incorrect because the spring constant is not a point on the graph. The spring constant is found from the gradient of the straight-line section (force per unit extension).

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A satellite orbits a planet in a circular path at constant speed.
  Which statement about the resultant force is correct?
options: A. No force acts because speed is constant.
B. The force is in the direction of motion.
C. The force is directed towards the centre of the orbit.
D. The force is directed away from the planet.
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • A satellite moving in a circle is constantly changing direction, even though its speed is constant
 • A change in direction means a change in velocity, so there must be a resultant force acting
 • That force is always directed towards the centre of the orbit — this is the centripetal force
 • It is provided by the gravitational pull of the planet
 A  is incorrect because a constant speed does not mean no force. The force changes the direction of motion, not the speed.
 B  is incorrect because a force in the direction of motion would cause the satellite to speed up, not travel in a circle.
 D  is incorrect because a force directed away from the planet would push the satellite outward, causing it to spiral away rather than orbit.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A ball is dropped from a height above the ground.
 Which transfer between energy stores takes place as the ball falls towards the ground?
options: A. chemical energy to kinetic energy
B. gravitational potential energy to elastic energy
C. kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy
D. gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • As the ball falls, it loses height, and therefore the energy in its gravitational potential store decreases
 • The ball speeds up, so the energy in its kinetic store increases
 • Therefore, the main transfer between energy stores is:
 gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy
 A  is incorrect because chemical energy is not involved in a falling ball. Chemical energy is stored in fuels, food and batteries.
 B  is incorrect because elastic energy is only relevant if the ball deforms (e.g. on impact with the ground), not during free fall through air.
 C  is incorrect because this describes the energy transfer for the opposite motion, i.e. a ball being thrown upwards into the air.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem: Which energy resource does  not  originate from the Sun's radiation?
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is A
 • Tidal energy comes from the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun on the oceans, not solar radiation
 B  is incorrect because wind is caused by differential solar heating.
 C  is incorrect because waves are generated by wind, which comes from solar heating.
 D  is incorrect because hydroelectric power depends on the water cycle, driven by solar evaporation.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A beaker of water is heated from room temperature until the water boils.
 Which statement about the water is correct?
options: A. The temperature of the water increases at a constant rate throughout the heating.
B. The temperature of the water increases until it boils, then continues to increase slowly.
C. The temperature of the water increases until it reaches 100 °C, then remains constant while it boils.
D. The water begins to boil as soon as heating starts.
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • When water is heated, its temperature rises as the internal energy of the water molecules increases
 • When the water reaches its boiling point (100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure), the temperature remains constant
 • At the boiling point, the energy supplied is used to break the intermolecular bonds and change the state from liquid to gas, rather than to increase the temperature
 • This is why the temperature stays at 100 °C until all the water has boiled
 A  is incorrect because the rate of temperature increase is not constant. It depends on the mass of water remaining and heat losses to the surroundings. More importantly, the temperature stops increasing entirely at the boiling point.
 B  is incorrect because the temperature does not continue to increase above the boiling point while liquid water is still present. All the energy goes into the change of state.
 D  is incorrect because boiling only occurs at the boiling point (100 °C), not at room tempe

 • Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules
 • When the temperature decreases, the average kinetic energy decreases, so the average speed of the molecules decreases
 • Slower molecules hit the walls of the balloon less frequently and with less force
 • This means the pressure decreases
 A  is incorrect because the average speed of the molecules is directly related to the temperature. If the temperature decreases, the average speed must also decrease.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
Smoke particles are observed through a microscope. The smoke particles are seen to move in random, rapid motion.
 What causes the smoke particles to move in this way?
options: Air currents push the smoke particles in different directions.
B. The smoke particles collide with each other and change direction.
C. The smoke particles are hit by fast-moving air molecules that cannot be seen.
D. The smoke particles are repelled by electric charges on the glass walls.
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • The random, rapid motion of smoke particles is called Brownian motion
 • It is caused by collisions between the relatively large smoke particles and the much smaller, fast-moving air molecules
 • The air molecules are too small to be seen through the microscope, but their effect is visible because they constantly bombard the smoke particles from all sides
 • The collisions are random and uneven, causing the smoke particles to change direction unpredictably
 A  is incorrect because air currents would cause all the smoke particles to move in the same general direction, not in random, rapid motion.
 B  is incorrect because the random motion is caused by collisions with invisible air molecules, not collisions between the smoke particles themselves. The smoke particles are too far apart to collide frequently.
 D  is incorrect because Brownian motion is not caused by electrostatic forces. It is a result of molecular bombardment.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A liquid evaporates from an open dish.
 Which change would increase the rate of evaporation?
options: B. covering the dish with a lid
C. decreasing the surface area of the liquid
D. blowing air across the surface of the liquid
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • Evaporation occurs when molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough energy to escape as a gas
 • Blowing air across the surface removes the vapour molecules from above the liquid, preventing them from returning to the liquid and allowing more molecules to escape
 • This increases the rate of evaporation
 A  is incorrect because cooling the liquid reduces the average kinetic energy of the molecules. Fewer molecules will have enough energy to escape from the surface, so the rate of evaporation decreases.
 B  is incorrect because covering the dish traps the vapour above the liquid. The vapour becomes saturated and molecules return to the liquid at the same rate as they leave, so the net rate of evaporation decreases.
 C  is incorrect because decreasing the surface area reduces the number of molecules at the surface that can escape. A larger surface area increases the rate of evaporation.

 • Diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle
 • Diffraction increases when:
 • the wavelength increases (or frequency decreases, since v = fλ and wave speed is constant)
 • the gap width decreases (becomes closer to the wavelength)
 • Maximum diffraction occurs when the gap width is approximately equal to the wavelength
 • Decreasing the frequency increases the wavelength, and making the gap narrower brings it closer to the wavelength — both changes increase diffraction

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • In a plane mirror, the image is formed the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front of it
 • After stepping back, the person is 3.0 m in front of the mirror
 • The image is therefore 3.0 m behind the mirror
 • The distance between the person and their image is:
 
 A  is incorrect because 3.0 m is only the distance from the person to the mirror, not from the person to their image.
 B  is incorrect because this would be the distance between the person and their image at the original position (2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0 m), before they stepped back.
 C  is incorrect because it adds the old distance to the new distance (2.0 + 3.0 = 5.0 m).

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:

 • The loudness of a sound is related to the amplitude of the sound wave
 • Reducing the loudness produces a quieter sound, which means the amplitude decreases
 • The pitch of a sound is related to the frequency of the sound wave
 • Lowering the pitch means the frequency decreases
 • Therefore, both the amplitude and the frequency decrease
 B  is incorrect because the frequency should decrease (lower pitch), not increase.
 C  is incorrect because the amplitude should decrease (quieter), not increase.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows the magnetic field pattern around a bar magnet.
 At which position is the magnetic field strongest?
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is A
 • The strength of a magnetic field is shown by the spacing of the field lines
 • Where the field lines are closest together, the field is strongest
 • Position A is closest to a pole of the magnet, where the field lines are most concentrated
 • The field is strongest near the poles of the magnet and weakest far from the magnet
 B  is incorrect because it is furthest from the magnet, where the field lines are widely spaced, and the field is at its weakest.
 C  is incorrect because it is midway between the poles, where the field lines are more spread out, and the field is weaker.
 D  is incorrect because although it is close to a pole (north), the lines are more concentrated at point A, so the magnetic field is slightly stronger at A.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A plastic rod is rubbed with a cloth. The rod becomes negatively charged.
 What has happened during the charging process?
options: A. Protons have been transferred from the rod to the cloth.
B. Electrons have been transferred from the rod to the cloth.
C. Protons have been transferred from the cloth to the rod.
D. Electrons have been transferred from the cloth to the rod.
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • When two materials are rubbed together, electrons are transferred from one material to the other
 • Only electrons can be transferred because they are on the outer shells of atoms and can be removed by friction
 • Protons cannot be transferred because they are fixed in the nucleus of the atom
 • The rod becomes negatively charged, which means it has gained electrons
 • Therefore, electrons have been transferred from the cloth to the rod
 A  is incorrect because protons cannot be removed from the nucleus by friction. Charging by friction always involves the transfer of electrons.
 B  is incorrect because if electrons moved from the rod to the cloth, the rod would lose negative charge and become positively charged, not negatively charged.
 C  is incorrect because protons are located in the nucleus of the atom and cannot be transferred by rubbing.

B. the energy transferred per unit charge in driving charge around a complete circuit
C. the force that pushes electrons through the circuit
D. the potential difference across the terminals of the battery when no current flows

The correct answer is B
 • The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a source is defined as the energy transferred per unit charge in driving charge around a complete circuit
 • It is measured in volts (V), where 1 V = 1 J/C
 • The e.m.f. represents the total energy the battery gives to each coulomb of charge
 A  is incorrect because this is the definition of current (  ), not e.m.f.
 C  is incorrect because, despite the word "force" in its name, e.m.f. is not a force. It is an energy transfer per unit charge. This is a common misconception.
 D  is incorrect because this describes the terminal potential difference when no current flows, which happens to equal the e.m.f. numerically. However, this is not the definition of e.m.f. — it is a consequence of there being no internal energy losses.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem: What is the purpose of a fuse in a mains electrical circuit?
options: A. to reduce the current flowing through the appliance
B. to increase the resistance of the circuit so the appliance works safely
C. to break the circuit if the current becomes too large
D. to prevent the voltage from becoming too high
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • A fuse is a safety device that protects the circuit and the appliance
 • It contains a thin wire that melts when the current exceeds the rated value
 • When the wire melts, the circuit is broken (the current stops flowing)
 • This prevents overheating and reduces the risk of fire
 • Note that in a mains circuit, the fuse is always placed in the live wire
 A  is incorrect because a fuse does not reduce the current. It either allows the current to flow normally or breaks the circuit completely. It does not limit or regulate the current.
 B  is incorrect because the purpose of a fuse is not to increase resistance. A fuse has a very low resistance during normal operation so that it does not affect the circuit.
 D  is incorrect because a fuse responds to excessive current, not voltage. It does not control or limit the voltage in a circuit.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
A magnet is pushed into a coil of wire connected to a centre-zero sensitive ammeter. The ammeter shows a negative reading, as shown in diagram 1.
 The magnet is then held stationary inside the coil.
  What does the ammeter read when the magnet is stationary, as shown in diagram 2?
options: C. a reading that slowly decreases to zero
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • An e.m.f. is only induced in the coil when there is a change in the magnetic field through the coil
 • Moving the magnet into the coil changes the magnetic flux through the coil, which induces an e.m.f. and causes a current to flow
 • When the magnet is stationary inside the coil, the magnetic field through the coil is not changing
 • No change in magnetic flux means no induced e.m.f. and therefore no current
 • The ammeter reads zero
 A  &  B  are incorrect because a constant reading would require a continuously changing magnetic field. A stationary magnet produces a constant (unchanging) field, which does not induce an e.m.f.
 C  is incorrect because there is no gradual decrease. The reading drops to zero as soon as the magnet stops moving, not gradually over time.

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem: Which list shows the correct order of the life cycle of a star like the Sun?
options: A. nebula → main sequence star → red supergiant → neutron star
B. nebula → main sequence star → red giant → white dwarf
C. nebula → red giant → main sequence star → white dwarf
D. main sequence star → nebula → red giant → black hole
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is B
 • A star like the Sun (a star of similar mass) follows this life cycle:
 • a nebula (cloud of gas and dust) collapses under gravity
 • nuclear fusion begins and the star becomes a stable main sequence star
 • when hydrogen fuel is exhausted, the star expands to become a red giant
 • the outer layers are expelled and the remaining core contracts to form a white dwarf
 • The white dwarf eventually cools and fades

set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.stem:
The light from distant galaxies is observed to be redshifted.
 Which statement correctly explains this observation?
options: A. Distant galaxies are hotter than nearby galaxies.
B. Distant galaxies are moving away from us, stretching the wavelength of the light.
C. Light loses energy as it travels through space, decreasing its frequency.
D. The Universe is contracting, compressing the wavelength of the light.
set-8/paper-2-mulitple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is B
 • Redshift is the increase in the observed wavelength (decrease in frequency) of light from distant galaxies
 • It occurs because the galaxies are moving away from us — the expansion of the Universe stretches the wavelength of the light
 • The faster a galaxy moves away, the greater the redshift
 • This is evidence that the Universe is expanding
 A  is incorrect because the colour shift is not caused by temperature. Redshift is a Doppler-type effect caused by the relative motion of the galaxy away from the observer.
 C  is incorrect because light does not lose energy as it travels through the vacuum of space. The frequency of light remains constant unless the source is moving relative to the observer.
 D  is incorrect because red-shift indicates that wavelengths are being stretched (increased), not compressed. If the Universe were contracting, we would observe blueshift (shorter wavelengths), not redshift.
